A scalable whole-cell biocatalytic process for food-compatible production of resolvin D5 using the edible mushroom Pleurotus ostreatus
works.abstract: Specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) actively promote the resolution of inflammation, but their scalable and food-compatible production remains challenging because current methods rely on multistep chemical synthesis, mammalian cells, purified enzymes, crude enzyme preparations, or recombinant microorganisms. Here, we developed a scalable, food-compatible submerged-cultured whole-cell biocatalytic process for the production of resolvin D5 (RvD5; 7S,17S-dihydroxydocosahexaenoic acid) from docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) using the edible mushroom Pleurotus ostreatus. Submerged-cultured P. ostreatus whole cells stereoselectively converted DHA to RvD5 via a 17S-hydroxydocosahexaenoic acid intermediate through an endogenous lipoxygenase (LOX)-mediated double-oxygenation pathway, without enzyme purification or heterologous gene expression. Optimization of submerged cultivation conditions (cultivation period and medium composition) increased RvD5 production by 2.1-fold, and subsequent optimization of whole-cell biotransformation parameters (temperature, pH, cell and substrate concentrations, polyvinylpyrrolidone and ethanol supplementation, reaction time, and agitation) resulted in an overall 13.4-fold increase relative to the initial conditions. Under the optimized flask-scale conditions, whole cells produced 2.14mM (0.77g/L) RvD5 from 2.5mM DHA with an 85.6% molar yield within 40min. The process was successfully scaled up to a 3.0-L stirred-tank bioreactor (1.0-L working volume), producing 2.08mM (0.75g/L) RvD5 with an 83.2% molar yield within 60min. The developed cultivation-based edible fungal whole-cell biocatalytic process integrates catalyst preparation, efficient RvD5 biosynthesis, and scalable bioprocessing, providing a practical strategy for the scalable biotechnological production of DHA-derived SPMs.

works.title: Science Does Not Run on Evidence Alone
works.abstract: Scientists take pride in producing knowledge and finding solutions. However, the impact and use they really have depend largely on something we rarely discuss in scientific journals: inspiration. Often, the ability to inspire is attributed to a few individuals with special talent. Looking at the evidence, this is hardly justified: psychological research describes inspiration as a defined and measurable construct with three characteristics - it is evoked, it is motivating, and it is transcendent. That it is evoked is the important part, because it means inspiration reaches a person from outside and somebody is supplying it. Therefore, here we argue that we can learn to do so and this is increasingly important. Inspiration is associated with the creativity and productivity of scientific work, with the success of scientific careers, and also with the way public opinion embraces scientific content and findings. So, what can we do? We suggest first of all measuring and counting inspiration, appreciating the work in which it actually happens, building a sense of belonging to and into science early, and most importantly: doing it ourselves.

works.title: A domain library approach for generating antibodies that recruit T-cells with enhanced cytotoxicity using new bispecific bivalent antibodies
works.abstract: Traditionally, enhancing the function of T cell-recruiting antibodies requires a labor-intensive two-step process: initial phage display screening for binding affinity and secondary screening for cytotoxic activity. In this study, we utilized the bispecific bivalent antibody framework 'BiBian' and combined VHH phage display with a domain library approach for the generation of antibodies that recruit T-cells, thereby facilitating this evolution. By leveraging the modular nature of the single-domain component, we bypassed the affinity pre-selection phase by directly grafting mutant VHH libraries onto the BiBian framework for immediate cytotoxicity screening. While conventional methods were limited to evaluating only six candidates for cytotoxicity out of 264 initial clones, this method enabled the direct functional assessment of all 264 clones. This comprehensive approach significantly reduced the risk of overlooking high-potency variants that may not exhibit a linear correlation between binding affinity and functional output. Ultimately, three antibodies identified via this method exhibited a lower IC 50 for cytotoxic activity (down to 0.05 nM) than the top-performing candidate obtained through traditional methods (0.30 nM). In this proof-of-concept study, this accelerated functional-first strategy enabled the rapid evaluation of candidate potency within the target bivalent format. While further validation across other targets and antibody formats will be required to confirm broader applicability, these findings highlight the potential of the Dolag-ArT strategy for direct functional screening.

works.title: Predicting Achievable Carboxylic Acid and Amino Acid Titers
works.abstract: Industrial fermentation offers a promising route to produce enantiopure, bio-based carboxylic acids and amino acids. To identify the techno-economic and environmental sustainability of biotechnological production routes, early-stage process design and assessment are generally performed. For industrial-scale sustainability, achieving a high product concentration (titer) is critical. However, methods for predicting achievable acid fermentation titers are constrained by a lack of both ex-ante correlations and industrial-scale data. Therefore, we introduce a novel method to estimate the achievable titer for carboxylic acids and amino acids, based solely on the pH-corrected hydrophobicity (log D o/w , derived from log P o/w and p K a ), irrespective of the microorganism used. By analyzing 58 high, literature-reported, titers for carboxylates and amino acids, we formulated a 3-parameter logistic upper-bound function that describes this hydrophobicity-titer relationship (asymptote: 205 ± 21 g L -1 , N = 23). The function describes an upper boundary for optimised processes rather than an expected titer for arbitrary conditions. This function was applied to estimate the achievable titers of malonic acid, glycolic acid, cis,cis ‑muconic acid, and butyric acid reaching up to 204, 204, 200, and 172 g L⁻¹ at pH 7 respectively, while their expected titer decreases to approximately 164, 163, 73, and 31 g L⁻¹ at pH 3. Literature titers for the same product and microorganism at two pH values confirm this direction. The empirical correlation obtained in this study enables rapid, physics-informed estimation of achievable acid fermentation titers. Therefore, this method supports more reliable ex-ante bioprocess assessment and may accelerate sustainable bio-based acid production.

works.title: Cooperative mutations reshape lid dynamics in thermophilic lipase LipT6 enhancing stability and biodiesel production
works.abstract: Enzymatic biodiesel production offers a sustainable alternative to chemical transesterification, but industrial application of lipases is limited by acidic pH and high alcohol concentrations. Here, we combined previously identified stabilizing mutations in the thermophilic lipase LipT6 from Geobacillus stearothermophilus T6 to generate the S5 variant (H86Y/E251C/A269T/G332C/R374W) and investigated the molecular basis of its improved performance. S5 retained 94% of its activity after 1h at pH 4.8, compared with 33% for wild-type LipT6, and increased conversion of waste chicken oil to fatty acid methyl esters from 30.4% to 71.3%. The variant also showed increased thermal stability under neutral, acidic, and ethanol-rich conditions. Its determined 2.4Å crystal structure closely matched the wild-type closed-lid conformation, with a Cα RMSD of 0.38Å, indicating that enhanced function did not result from major structural rearrangements. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed conformation-dependent effects: wild-type and S5 behaved similarly in the closed state, whereas S5 exhibited greater lid flexibility and broader conformational sampling in the open state. Back-to-wild-type reversions in silico produced distinct shifts in lid sampling, supporting a cooperative contribution of the engineered mutations. Structural analysis further suggested that H86Y alters the environment of the Zn²⁺-binding region and adjacent lid hinge, while core mutations provide complementary stabilization. These findings demonstrate that cooperative engineering of core stability and lid dynamics can improve lipase performance under biodiesel-relevant conditions.

Machine learning-guided dual optimization of the substrate specificity and thermostability of yeast alcohol dehydrogenase
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Yeast alcohol dehydrogenase I (YADH) catalyzes the reversible reduction of aldehydes to primary alcohols. Thermostable YADH variants with broad substrate specificities at elevated temperatures are desirable for industrial biocatalysis. In this study, we aimed to alter the substrate specificity of YADH to efficiently catalyze the reduction of the non-native substrate, trans-2-nonenal, to trans-2-nonenol, while simultaneously enhancing thermostability. Residues around the substrate-binding site were identified by docking simulation and subjected to saturation and random mutagenesis. Measured activity and thermostability were used to train a machine-learning model to predict YADH variants with improved activity while maintaining thermostability. RESULTS: The machine learning-guided approach identified variants with improved properties. Four variants showed increased specific activity toward trans-2-nonenal compared with the wild type, and one variant also exhibited improved thermostability. The best-performing variant showed a more than twofold increase in specific activity along with retained thermal resistance. Variants that lost activity toward the native substrate acetaldehyde while gaining higher activity toward trans-2-nonenal were also obtained, indicating altered substrate specificity. These results demonstrate efficient identification of beneficial mutations from a limited dataset. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, this study presents a machine learning-guided framework that integrates docking and multi-model evaluation for simultaneously optimizing substrate specificity and thermostability in YADH.

works.title: Biosynthesis of valuable blue pigments: Recent advances, applications and perspectives
Engineering Methylobacterium as a C1 biomanufacturing platform: Metabolic architecture, regulatory networks, and synthetic biology strategies
Advances and challenges in the prediction of atom transition maps
works.abstract: Understanding how complex phenotypes emerge from large-scale biochemical networks necessitates accurate representation of biochemical reactions that extend beyond mass and charge balances. Atom transition maps provide atom-level representation of biochemical reactions that facilitate discovery of design principles in biochemical networks and, in combination with labeling experiments, enable flux estimation. In this systematic review, we categorize, compare, and contrast the existing computational approaches for the prediction of atom transition maps both on the level of individual reactions as well as entire biochemical networks. Emphasis is placed on the growing number of approaches that predict atom transition maps using deep learning alone or in combination with conventional optimization-based approaches. We stress the problems of data leakage typically arising in prediction of atom transition maps using the existing machine and deep learning approaches for reactions that share mechanisms. Importantly, we illustrate the severity of the problem by re-examining representative deep learning models for the prediction of atom transition maps on a unified test set of reactions. The review of these advances alongside our comparative analysis points at open problems in generation of atom transition maps and paves the way for future research in this area.

works.title: Improving Whole‐Cell Taxifolin Production Performance Through Growth‐coupled Directed Laboratory Evolution of Flavanone 3‐hydroxylase in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The unique hydroxylation pattern confers dihydroflavonols with multiple beneficial functions to human health. The bioproduction of dihydroflavonols is strictly driven by flavanone 3‐hydroxylase (F3H. This study focused on producing taxifolin, a typical high‐value dihydroflavonol. We established taxifolin synthesis route by substituting the plant‐derived flavonoid 3’‐hydroxylase (F3’H) with prokaryote‐derived two‐component 4HPA3H system (HpaB and HpaC). Kinetics of the production indicated that F3H is the rate‐limiting node. A directed library evolution (DLE) method was proposed to debottleneck this route. The tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle was rebuilt in Escherichia coli to couple DLE with cell growth. Very high transformation efficiency was achieved after medium optimization, thus facilitating the mutant library building. A library, theoretically containing 42360 mutants, was built and underwent a 4‐day DLE. Among the randomly picked out mutants, SlF3H v01 showed significantly accelerated catalytic rate. The whole‐cell containing SlF3H v01 produced 301.28% more taxifolin (93.82 mg/L) at 22 h and 29.73% more taxifolin (119.87 mg/L) at 46 h than that containing the wild type. This study built an E. coli chassis and developed an easy‐to‐manipulate DLE method to improve the taxifolin production. It can also be expanded to improve the performance of whole‐cell catalyst or microbial cell factory containing other α‐ketoglutarate‐dependent dioxygenase.

works.title: Comparison of Wildtype and Recombinant Adeno‐Associated Virus (AAV) Production Reveals Distinct Productivity and Content Ratio Profiles
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Recombinant adeno‐associated virus is a leading viral vector for gene therapy. However, recombinant adeno‐associated virus production systems have low titer and content ratio (ratio of genome‐containing to total adeno‐associated virus capsids), making it difficult to generate the large number of vector genomes required for clinical or commercial use. In contrast, wildtype adeno‐associated virus achieves over ten‐fold higher titer compared to recombinant adeno‐associated virus and a content ratio of over 95% full. Despite the higher productivity of wildtype adeno‐associated virus, the mechanisms behind its productivity remain poorly understood. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel wildtype adeno‐associated virus production platform in suspension human embryonic kidney cells across varying multiplicities of infection of adeno‐associated virus to adenovirus. The impact of cellular viral genome delivery mechanisms and the interplay between adeno‐associated virus and its adenoviral helper were investigated by comparing infection‐based systems with transfection‐based and infection–transfection hybrid systems. Wildtype and hybrid infection systems had remarkably different host cell growth profiles and viral gene expression patterns, and achieved over a log‐fold higher titers and 45% higher content ratios, reaching 8.1 × 10 12 vector genomes/mL culture and 72.2% full, compared to recombinant transfection systems (1.63 × 10 11 vector genomes/mL and 26.9% full).

works.title: Nuclear Functional Divergence and Genetic Basis of Cap Colour Variation Revealed by T2T Genomes of Two Compatible Monokaryons in Pholiota adiposa
works.abstract: Basidiomycete fungi maintain a dikaryotic state throughout their life cycle, in which two genetically distinct haploid nuclei coexist within the same cytoplasm. However, the extent and functional significance of inter-nuclear genomic divergence remain poorly understood. Here, we present the first telomere-to-telomere assemblies of two compatible monokaryons (D1 and D11) from a wild isolate of Pholiota adiposa, achieving 13 complete chromosomes with zero gaps and Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs completeness of 98.6% and 98.3%, substantially outperforming the previous fragmented assembly. The two nuclei exhibit only 75% collinear genes, with 570 (D1) and 668 (D11) strain-specific genes. D1-specific genes are enriched in energy metabolism, consistent with faster mycelial growth, while D11-specific genes are enriched in genetic information processing and mitogen-activated protein kinase signalling, revealing functional complementarity between the two haploid nuclei. Resequencing of 18 wild accessions identified two candidate regions associated with red pileus colour on chromosomes 6 and 12, the former as a major-effect locus and the latter harbouring multiple pigment-associated genes. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment implicated phenylalanine metabolism, tyrosine metabolism, and terpenoid biosynthesis in colour formation, suggesting coordinated regulation across metabolic networks. This framework facilitates dissection of nuclear functional divergence and provides candidate targets for understanding fungal phenotypic variation.

works.title: Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against Fusarium oxysporum: biocontrol, metabolites, and simvastatin docking
works.abstract: This study demonstrates the considerable antagonistic activity of Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against a pathogenic Fusarium oxysporum AUMC3191 isolate. In dual culture assay, soil-isolated Aspergillus terreus Thom effectively hindered F. oxysporum AUMC3191 growth and impressively blocked zearalenone (ZEN) synthesis. Scanning electron microscopy demonstrated significant damage to F. oxysporum hyphae, such as abnormalities, shrinkage, bending, and deformity. Molecular identification through rDNA ITS sequence analysis confirmed the isolate as Aspergillus terreus, registered in GeneBank (Accession No. OR480103). GC/MS profiling of A. terreus MAK153 identified several bioactive secondary metabolites, notably estragole, caryophyllene, 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol, 1-docosene, 1-docosanol, olean-12-ene-3,28-diol, and simvastatin. Statistical analysis revealed a very strong positive correlation (r = 0.99) between chromatographic peak area% and peak area values. The influence of nutrient sources on simvastatin production was evaluated using four culture media. FTIR and HPLC analyses confirmed simvastatin biosynthesis, while HPLC revealed significant medium-dependent variation in yield (p < 0.001). Camellia sinensis Tea broth (CTB) elicited the highest yield, dominating extracellular filtrate accumulation (145.93 ± 1.13 mg/mL). Molecular docking simulations assessed simvastatin's binding affinity to HMG-CoA reductase and 3-ketosteroid reductase, yielding binding energies of -8.0 and -7.8 kcal/mol, respectively. The interactions involved multiple hydrophobic bonds and hydrogen bonds, suggesting simvastatin functions as a multi-target inhibitor capable of disrupting ergosterol biosynthesis at two distinct sites. Notably, this study represents the first computational exploration of simvastatin's interaction with 3-ketosteroid reductase, with implications for estrogen signalling modulation and potential therapeutic applications. KEY POINTS: • Aspergillus terreus MAK153 inhibits F. oxysporum growth and zearalenone production • Aspergillus terreus induces significant hyphal damage in F. oxysporum using SEM • Simvastatin-HMG-CoA and 3-ketosteroid interaction could modulate estrogen-related pathways potentially.

works.title: Next-generation precision fermentation: integrating engineered cell factories, bioprocess intensification, and smart bioprocessing
works.abstract: Precision fermentation (PF) uses engineered microbial cell factories to manufacture defined products under controlled bioprocess conditions. In this review, PF is treated operationally as the integration of engineered hosts with metabolic engineering and process control, while traditional food fermentations without engineered production strains are excluded. The field now spans pharmaceuticals, food ingredients, industrial enzymes, specialty chemicals, and biopolymers, but commercial translation remains constrained by biological non-linearity, substrate and feedstock variability, mass-transfer limitations at scale, downstream recovery, and the cost gap with incumbent processes. This mini-review examines five connected layers: engineered microbial chassis; design build test learn (DBTL) and multi-omics-guided metabolic engineering; bioreactor intensification; Process Analytical Technology (PAT), soft sensors and AI-enabled control; and techno-economic and life cycle assessment. Quantitative case studies illustrate both the progress and the remaining scale-up gaps, including semi-synthetic artemisinin, recombinant insulin, lactic acid, succinic acid, QS-21, and polyhydroxyalkanoates. The central argument is that the next phase of PF will depend less on isolated improvements in strain performance than on coordinated integration of strain design, intensified operation, real-time process understanding, and rigorous economic and environmental assessment. This integration is essential for translating laboratory performance into reproducible, scalable, and commercially credible biomanufacturing. KEY POINTS: PF requires integration of cell-factory engineering with scalable bioprocessing rather than optimisation of any single layer. DBTL and multi-omics improve strain performance, but laboratory titres do not guarantee industrial scalability. Bioprocess intensification and real-time monitoring are required to convert strain performance into robust production. PAT, soft sensors, and AI strengthen process control when supported by reliable online data and qualified models. TEA and LCA should be integrated early to filter commercial and environmental feasibility before scale-up.

works.title: Corrigendum to “HIV-Gag VLP-based vaccine purification at manufacturing scale: Combination of counterflow centrifugation and nuclease treatment as a key to DNA depletion” [New Biotechnol. 93 (2026) 264–279/ISSN 1871–6784]
Identification of ferulic acid tolerance targets in engineered Komagataella phaffii by transcriptomics-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling
works.abstract: Ferulic acid (FA) is an abundant aromatic precursor in lignocellulosic biomass and a promising substrate for vanillin biosynthesis, but its toxicity limits microbial conversion at elevated concentrations. Komagataella phaffii is a widely used non-conventional yeast cell factory with favorable properties for aromatic compound production, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying FA tolerance in this host remain poorly understood. An engineered K. phaffii strain carrying a heterologous FA-to-vanillin pathway was exposed to 20 mM FA under non-induced (FE–NI) and methanol-induced (FE-I) conditions. Both conditions exhibited higher growth rates and final cell densities compared with the wild-type, with FE-I exhibiting active FA catabolism and transient vanillin accumulation. Notably, FE–NI achieved comparable tolerance without detectable FA consumption, indicating that metabolic reprogramming of the host cell contributes to FA tolerance. Transcriptomic profiling revealed condition-dependent stress responses: FE–NI activated a host-level program comprising cell surface reinforcement, mitochondrial energy and redox support, and central carbon remodeling, whereas FE-I coupled active FA conversion with enhanced aldehyde detoxification and sugar-metabolism remodeling. Candidate tolerance targets were prioritized by integrating transcriptome data with a genome-scale metabolic model using an E-Flux approach. Functional validation by overexpression in the wild-type strain identified AGC1 and PAS_chr3_0834 as the most effective targets under non-induced and methanol-induced conditions, with colony number increasing 7.4-fold and 4.0-fold relative to the control, respectively. Co-expression of AGC1 and PAS_chr3_0834 increased biomass accumulation relative to the wild-type but did not exceed the effect of AGC1 alone under the tested condition. This study reveals condition-dependent FA tolerance programs in engineered K. phaffii and shows that integrating transcriptomics with genome-scale metabolic modeling can facilitate the identification of tolerance targets. The validated targets represent valuable engineering options for improving the robustness of K. phaffii cell factories employed in FA-based aromatic compound bioconversion.

works.title: Fibroproliferative Remodeling of Immune‐Vascular Co‐Culture Spheroid Models in Response to Atherogenic Stimulation
works.abstract: Cell-based models are highly valuable platforms for preclinical studies of atherosclerosis, offering controllable environments to investigate disease mechanisms. Three-dimensional (3D) spheroids, a class of cell-based models, enable the study of atherosclerotic disease phenomena under physiologically relevant yet controlled conditions. In this study, we examined the lipid-induced changes in a co-culture spheroid model comprising THP-1-derived macrophages and primary human coronary artery smooth muscle cells (HCASMCs) following treatment with 20 or 40 µg/mL oxidized LDL (ox-LDL), a known atherogenic agent. Over a 10-day period, we assessed changes in spheroid morphology (size and compactness), cell viability, metabolic activity, intracellular composition, gene expression, pro-inflammatory cytokine release and extracellular matrix deposition, relative to the untreated control. Lipid exposure increased the abundance of macrophages in ox-LDL-treated spheroids (LS20-3 h: 35.5 ± 21.9%; LS40-3 h: 38.3 ± 8.7%) compared with controls (21.8 ± 0.7%) as early as day 3. Upregulation of fibronectin (LS20-3 h: ~1.8-fold; LS40-3 h: ~2.1-fold), CD36 (~1.8-fold), and ABCA-1 (~1.9-fold) was also observed. Moreover, spheroids exposed to 40 µg/mL ox-LDL exhibited reduced viability and compactness compared with those treated with 20 µg/mL by day 10. While lipid-treated spheroids showed non-statistically significantly higher levels of pro-inflammatory IL-1β cytokine expression at day 0 which declined (> 85% decrease) by day 3, all spheroid groups showed comparable global fibronectin ECM secretion indices. Collectively, these findings reveal lipid-induced proliferative changes to spheroid composition & functionality and show their potential as biomimetic models for the study of atherosclerotic disease phenomena.

works.title: Cac3319 Inactivation Sustains Solventogenesis Through Proteomic and Phosphoregulatory Remodeling in Clostridium acetobutylicum
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Clostridium acetobutylicum is a promising biofuel producer for acetone‐butanol‐ethanol (ABE) fermentation, yet sustained butanol production is constrained by the short duration of solventogenic activity. Although the orphan histidine kinase Cac3319 has been implicated in Spo0A phosphorylation, sporulation, and solvent production, metabolic and phosphorylation changes following cac3319 inactivation have not been systematically characterized. Here, we integrated fermentation kinetics, comparative proteomics, and Ti 4+ ‐IMAC phosphoproteomics to investigate the effects of cac3319 inactivation in C. acetobutylicum ATCC 55025. The cac3319 knockout prolonged late‐stage metabolic activity without impairing early growth, enabling continued glucose utilization and solvent accumulation after entry into solventogenesis. Final butanol and total ABE titers increased from 13.0 to 17.5 g L −1 and from 18.5 to 28.5 g L −1 , respectively. Proteomic analysis revealed increased protein abundance spanning central carbon metabolism, acid reassimilation, energy metabolism, and protein protection. Phosphoproteomic analysis further revealed phase‐dependent remodeling of detectable phosphorylation events, indicating that post‐translational regulation was reshaped during the acidogenic‐to‐solventogenic transition. These coordinated changes supported a metabolically active and stress‐tolerant state conducive to sustained solventogenesis. Collectively, these findings provide new insights into histidine kinase‐mediated regulation of clostridial solventogenesis and highlight cac3319 inactivation as a promising strategy for sustaining late‐stage metabolic activity and improving butanol production in ABE fermentation.

works.title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence‐Driven Neutrosophic Multi‐Objective Optimization of Oxygen Transfer Systems in Smart Bioreactors
works.abstract: Oxygen transfer control in industrial bioreactors becomes more complex when cell metabolic changes, nonlinear process dynamics, energy constraints, and biological and operational uncertainties simultaneously affect control decisions. This study presents an innovative framework for intelligent oxygenation management that integrates a synchronized digital twin, agent-based artificial intelligence, fuzzy-notrosophic modeling, and multi-objective decision-making in a closed, uncertainty-aware loop. The proposed framework enables predictive and safe decision-making under variable conditions by continuously monitoring and reconstructing the process state, predicting short-term behavior, generating and screening control options, and virtually evaluating them before implementation. Evaluation under normal operating conditions and biological and process disturbances showed that the complete framework achieved 98.04% dissolved oxygen stability and reduced the recovery time after oxygen demand shock to 7.26 min. The findings show that the main value of this architecture lies not in the single maximization of oxygen transfer, but in creating an adaptive balance between oxygen delivery, energy consumption, shear stress, biological stability, and operational risk. This framework provides an extensible platform for moving toward autonomous, resilient, and sustainable bioreactors.

works.title: Yeast Surface Display of Artificial Multienzyme Complexes for Enhanced Production of Rebaudioside M
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Rebaudioside M (Reb M) is an ideal low‐calorie natural sweetener with excellent sensory properties and well‐established safety profile. Industrial production of Reb M is limited by low natural abundance and the bottlenecks of existing biomanufacturing strategies, including low productivity, intermediate accumulation and high enzyme costs. Here, a novel biosynthetic platform based on yeast surface display of artificial multienzyme complexes was established for efficient Reb M production. The artificial protein scaffold containing multiple orthogonal cohesin modules was displayed on the surface of Pichia pastoris via the AGA1 anchoring motif. Through orthogonal cohesin‐dockerin interactions, Reb M biosynthetic pathway enzymes (PgUGT Mut , AtSUS1 and UGT76G1 Mut ) with the corresponding dockerin modules were assembled on the artificial protein scaffold to form multienzyme complexes. The catalytic activity of crude glycosyltransferases was improved by isozyme screening and expression optimization with molecular chaperones. This surface‐displayed system demonstrated multiple advantages. First, the multienzyme complex assembled on the yeast surface showed higher catalytic efficiency than free enzymes. Additionally, fructose was consumed by P. pastoris to drive the reaction toward Reb M biosynthesis. Furthermore, the whole‐cell catalyst showed promising reusability. Ultimately, this platform enabled the production of 36.88 g/L Reb M with a yield of 91.9% from rebaudioside A (Reb A) in a 10 mL reaction system. This work provided a feasible strategy to address the key bottlenecks in Reb M biomanufacturing and offered a reference for producing other high‐value natural products via multi‐enzyme cascade catalysis.

works.title: Kinetics Based on the Rapid‑Equilibrium Approach for the Reduction of an Achiral Ketone to a Chiral Alcohol by a Single Carbonyl Reductase With NAD(P)H Regeneration Using Isopropyl Alcohol as the Hydrogen Donor
works.abstract: The kinetics of a single-enzyme, substrate-coupled system in batch operation for the asymmetric production of chiral alcohols from achiral ketones through NAD(P)H regeneration-using isopropyl alcohol (IPA) as a hydrogen donor-were investigated. Assuming the effective removal of acetone, two novel mathematical equations were derived by applying the rapid equilibrium approach to four enzyme-substrate complexes: one for the chiral alcohol formation rate, and another modeling its concentration over time under the assumption of a constant IPA concentration. The formation rate equation for batch operation was transformed into a dimensionless form to elucidate how constituent variables and parameters affect the reaction rate. The derived rate equations, which are two-parameter mathematical models, are substantially simpler than those in previously reported studies. The derived product formation rate decreases monotonically and remarkably with reaction time, agreeing with experimental results reported across the literature. The proposed time-course equation was validated against experimental data from two published studies. The fit of the derived equations to the experimental data was satisfactory within acceptable deviations, provided the core assumptions were satisfied.

works.title: Batch‐to‐Batch Optimization of pH Shifts in CHO Bioreactor Operations
works.abstract: Culture pH is an important operating parameter in CHO cell cultures producing mAb since it directly affects growth and specific productivity. Mathematical models can be used to optimize the magnitude and timing of pH shifts provided that they are robust to model errors. To address model errors, we implement, for the first time experimentally, a robust batch-to-batch optimization procedure that iteratively adjusts the model by updating model parameters and by matching predicted to measured gradients of the objective function and constraints at each iteration. A dynamic metabolic flux model with pH-dependent kinetic constraints was used for optimization. The approach was applied experimentally using a system of micro-bioreactors, leading to an improvement of the titer up to 18% compared to the nominal experimental conditions. The necessity of gradient matching to compensate for model errors was clearly demonstrated by comparing experiments conducted with and without gradient matching. The mathematical model also allowed the identification of metabolic mechanisms that contribute to the observed improvements in productivity.

works.title: Metabolic Remodelingof the NOG Pathway and Glyoxylate Cycle for High‐Yield L‐Homoserine Biosynthesis
works.abstract: L‑homoserine is a valuable C4 amino acid with broad applications in agriculture, pharmaceuticals, and daily chemicals. However, existing high‑yielding strains have mainly been evaluated at laboratory scale, and their scale‑up feasibility has not yet been sufficiently verified, leaving industrial production without a direct engineering basis. In this study, a non-auxotrophic, scalable L‑homoserine high‑producer was constructed by targeting carbon loss, rewiring the metabolic network, and maintaining cofactor balance. Specifically, the threonine branch was dynamically attenuated to reduce product degradation, while the non‑oxidative glycolysis (NOG) pathway was introduced and coupled with the glyoxylate shunt to conserve carbon and redirect flux toward the aspartate pathway, thereby increasing precursor availability. The main biosynthetic pathway and cofactor regeneration were further strengthened to accelerate L‑homoserine synthesis. Ultimately, strain HS25 achieved a titer of 126.5 g/L L‑homoserine,a yield of 0.58 g/g glucose, and a productivity of 1.77 g/L/hin 50 L fermentation. These metabolic engineering strategies are scalable and may serve as a generalizable framework for the industrial production of other aspartate‑derived amino acids and their derivatives.

works.title: 10‐Fold Improvement in Depth Filter Capacity During Integrated Dynamic Bioprocessing (IDB) Purification Through Depth Filter Cycling and Precipitate Control Strategy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT During bsAb1 purification, precipitate was formed during neutralization of the affinity capture product. This precipitate was removed before loading onto the first polishing column in the Integrated Dynamic Bioprocessing (IDB) platform. The precipitate had a dynamic particle size distribution that caused complex scaling without proper characterization. Herein, the study established a protocol for characterizing downstream precipitate formation and operating a depth filter (Emphaze AEX) like a chromatography column to support continuous purification of bsAb1. The depth filter is “underloaded” with precipitated material, followed by a chase step and the application of sanitization buffers. The sanitization buffers solubilized precipitate bound to the depth filter and controlled bioburden, drastically increasing the filter capacity and helped ensure a closed system. At the bench, the depth filter was cycled 40 times for a total capacity of 10,500 L/m 2 . This capacity is an order of magnitude greater than when the depth filter is loaded to max capacity without any cycling or sanitization. The resulting cycling capacity eases depth filter scale‐up and IDB implementation at the clinical and commercial scale.

A mosaic T7 phage platform enables simultaneous display of two independent peptides on the same phage particle. The modular design integrates receptor targeting, protein capture, and tissue-directed in vivo phage display, establishing a versatile methodology for multifunctional phage engineering, receptor identification, and next-generation combinatorial library design.

works.title: An mRNA–lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection
works.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

works.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo
Systems biology and synthetic engineering of probiotic yeasts
Improved Biosynthesis of Ethylene Glycol From Xylose in Engineered E. coli Utilizing Two‐Stage Dynamic Control
works.abstract: ABSTRACT We engineered Escherichia coli for improved ethylene glycol (EG) biosynthesis using two‐stage dynamic metabolic control coupled with pathway optimization. An engineered Dahms pathway ( xylB, xylC, xylD, yqhD ) was induced upon phosphate depletion to enable EG biosynthesis during stationary phase. The performance of our initial strain, expressing a baseline pathway, was improved by the addition of “stoichiometric” valves enabling proteolytic degradation of xylose isomerase and soluble transhydrogenase, upon phosphate depletion. Reduction of these enzymes, which compete for substrates with EG biosynthesis, led to a 3‐fold increase in specific productivity. In contrast, enabling “regulatory” dynamic metabolic valves targeting enoyl‐ACP reductase and glucose‐6‐phosphate dehydrogenase, designed to enhance NADPH flux, did not improve production in this control. Following pathway optimization, regulatory strains exhibited enhanced production rates exceeding 0.5 g gCDW − 1 h − 1 , a 14‐fold improvement over the control, while stoichiometric valves conferred no benefit. Scale‐up in fed‐batch bioreactors achieved 140 g L − 1 EG in 70 h with a yield of 0.38 g g − 1 xylose (92% of theoretical), representing one of the highest reported titers in E. coli . These results demonstrate that optimal engineering strategies shift with pathway capacity. While elimination of competing fluxes benefits low‐flux systems, high‐flux pathways require enhanced cofactor regeneration.

works.title: Engineering Mosaic T7 Bacteriophages for Dual Peptide Display to Enable Cellular Targeting and Ligand‐Directed Protein Capture
works.abstract: Integrating molecular recognition, tracing, and interactome capture within a single nanoparticle could allow for probing, manipulation, and control of complex biological systems. Achieving such multifunctionality within a single well-defined nanostructure remains challenging. T7 bacteriophage-based biological nanoparticles provide a robust and genetically programmable scaffold; however, conventional T7 display systems typically accommodate only one exogenous peptide species per phage particle, limiting multifunctional and combinatorial applications. Here, we describe a mosaic phage platform that enables the simultaneous display of two peptides on separate T7 coat protein subunits. By combining genome-encoded and plasmid-driven expression of peptide-fused capsid proteins, the system provides a modular route for assembling multifunctional phage nanoparticles. We generated mosaic T7 phages co-presenting the neuropilin-1 (NRP-1)-binding peptide RPARPAR alongside either a HA-tag or a Twin-Strep (Tstrep) tag affinity handle. These engineered phages specifically target NRP-1-expressing cells and enable immunofluorescence visualization and pull-down of NRP-1 from complex lysates. Furthermore, a random peptide T7 phage library co-displaying the constant lung-homing peptide RPARPAR shows preferential pulmonary accumulation in vivo, demonstrating utility for combinatorial targeting and tissue-directed phage selection. Collectively, this dual-display approach expands phage display by enabling cell targeting, visualization, molecular interactome probing, and in vivo tissue homing within a single genetically encoded nanoparticle platform.

works.title: Issue Information: Biotechnology Journal 11/2026
ARTP Mutagenesis and Omics‐Guided Target Validation for Improved Human Serum Albumin Fusion Protein Production in Yeast
works.abstract: Efficient production of human serum albumin (HSA) fusion proteins in yeast remains constrained by the combined demands of folding, secretion, and cellular resource allocation. Rational optimization of endoplasmic reticulum folding and unfolded protein response pathways can improve production, but additional cellular constraints may persist in engineered strains. Here, we combined iterative atmospheric and room-temperature plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, activity-coupled screening, and genome- and transcriptome-guided validation to improve production of an amylase-HSA fusion protein (AGSH) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Using extracellular α-amylase activity as the screening indicator, five rounds of ARTP mutagenesis in the folding-optimized strain AH28 generated mutants with enhanced AGSH production. The final mutant N5S14 reached 2.12-fold the AH28 level in AGSH-associated α-amylase activity. Physiological profiling showed that enhanced production was associated with altered growth-production balance and changes in glucose, ethanol, and glycerol profiles. Whole-genome sequencing identified 33 candidate mutation sites, and reverse engineering validated genes associated with improved AGSH production, including BUD27, NPR3, NPR2, and IML1. RNA-seq revealed distinct transcriptional states involving central carbon metabolism, protein folding, and stress-related processes. Transcriptome-guided validation identified PFY1 deletion and SSA3 overexpression as additional beneficial interventions. Overall, this strategy improved AGSH production and identified engineering targets beyond previously optimized folding-related modules.

YlYxc1, an ER-associated alkaline ceramidase of Yarrowia lipolytica, has the hydrolytic activity of ceramides, which can be exploited as a metabolic engineering target to enhance long-chain base production.

works.title: Progress in the microbial synthesis and biomedical applications of silver and gold nanoparticles
works.abstract: Abstract Nanoscience has revolutionized materials synthesis, with noble metal nanoparticles like silver and gold gaining prominence for their unique physicochemical and biological properties. Microbial synthesis offers a sustainable, biocompatible alternative to conventional methods, leveraging bacteria, fungi, and algae as natural biofactories to produce stable silver and gold nanoparticles via enzymatic reduction and biomolecule-mediated capping. Here, we review mechanisms of microbial nanoparticle biosynthesis, characterization techniques, and diverse biomedical applications, including antimicrobial, anticancer, antioxidant, drug-delivery, imaging, and wound-healing functionalities. However, despite their promise, challenges related to toxicity, consistency, process scalability, batch-to-batch variation, and regulatory compliance remain significant concerns. Thus, a thorough assessment of nanoparticle physicochemical properties, biosafety, and therapeutic effectiveness is crucial to advance clinical applications. Overall, microbial nanotechnology offers a promising avenue for biomedical use, but further refinement and standardized assessments are needed to enable reliable, scalable applications. Key points Microbial synthesis of silver and gold nanoparticles is sustainable and biocompatible.Diverse microorganisms act as natural nanofactories capable of producing stable AgNPs and AuNPs.Silver and gold nanoparticles exhibit broad biomedical potential.

works.title: Multilevel metabolic engineering of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens for enhanced L-tyrosine production
Functional Characterization and Application of Yarrowia lipolytica YlYxc1 for Enhanced Production of Sphingoid Bases
works.abstract: Long-chain bases (LCBs; sphingoid bases), derived from ceramide metabolism, are valuable sphingolipid intermediates for industrial applications. Here, we functionally characterized a putative ceramidase from Yarrowia lipolytica (YlYxc1) and evaluated its potential to enhance LCB production. YlYxc1 contains a conserved alkaline ceramidase motif with seven transmembrane helices and shares ~42% amino acid identity with Saccharomyces cerevisiae alkaline ceramidases ScYpc1 and ScYdc1. Despite lacking a canonical ER retention motif, YlYxc1 localized to the ER membrane. Deletion of YlYXC1 caused no major growth or lipid profile changes. Heterologous overexpression of YlYXC1 in S. cerevisiae wild-type and Scypc1Δydc1Δ strains increased phytosphingosine (PHS) production over dihydrosphingosine (DHS), mimicking ScYPC1 overexpression. In vitro activity assays using microsomal fractions from Scypc1Δydc1Δ cells expressing YlYXC1 revealed preferential hydrolysis of phytoceramide with an alkaline pH optimum. Furthermore, YlYXC1 expression in an engineered Y. lipolytica strain expressing heterologous acetyltransferases WcSLI1 and WcATF2 remarkably enhanced acetylated LCB production. Multi-copy integration of YlYXC1 into the Ylsur2Δsld1Δ strain also increased the secretory production of non-acetylated DHS. These findings establish YlYxc1 as a promising metabolic engineering target for producing value-added LCBs for pharmaceutical and cosmeceutical applications.

works.title: Issue Information
Duplex qPCR for detection and discrimination of wild-type and persistent O foot-and-mouth disease virus
works.abstract: Abstract Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), predominantly caused by serotype O foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV), remains highly contagious and economically devastating worldwide. A significant challenge in disease control is that recovered or vaccinated animals can become asymptomatic carriers of persistent strains (Op), which are indistinguishable from acute wild-type (WT) strains using current diagnostic methods. In this study, we developed a duplex TaqMan real-time PCR assay based on comparative next-generation sequencing and genomic analysis of WT and persistent O FMDV strains. Conserved regions were identified for universal detection, and Op-specific single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) mutations were targeted for differential amplification using ARMS-PCR (amplification refractory mutation system PCR). The optimized assay, consisting of a co-detection channel and a typing channel, demonstrated excellent specificity with no cross-reactivity against host nucleic acids or unrelated cell lines, a detection limit of 5 copies/µL, and clear differentiation of WT from Op strains. Furthermore, the duplex assay successfully distinguished wild-type and persistent strains in infected cell samples and across different viral passages (PI30 and PI60). This duplex TaqMan RT-qPCR assay provides, for the first time, a sensitive, specific, and efficient tool for simultaneous detection and differentiation of wild-type and persistent O FMDV strains in infected cell samples and across viral passages. Although clinical validation remains to be performed, this assay offers a promising basis for further studies on FMD surveillance and the detection of viral persistence. Key points • First duplex TaqMan RT-qPCR assay differentiating wild-type and persistent O FMDV. • Detection limit of 5 copies/µL with no cross-reactivity against host nucleic acids. • Differentiates Op strains at passages 30 and 60, monitors persistence, aids control.

works.title: Enhanced violacein production by synthetically engineered mutualistic Escherichia coli co-culture biofilms in a spatially partitioned bioreactor system
works.abstract: Violacein (VIO) is a bacterial secondary metabolite with potential applications in healthcare, textile, and cosmetic industries. Although modular synthetic E. coli co-cultures are promising for biomanufacturing, VIO production in such systems depends on efficient cross-feeding, which requires spatial proximity and stable interactions among co-culture members. Here, we demonstrate that a spatially partitioned bioreactor can support coexisting suspended and carrier-associated states of a mutualistic recombinant E. coli co-culture, enabling direct comparison of their crude VIO production performance. The co-culture was cultivated in a spatially partitioned bioreactor consisting of an aerobic stirred-tank compartment connected to an oxygen-limited cartridge containing Fibra-Cel® discs as carriers, thereby enabling biomass partitioning into suspended and adherent fractions. Across three biological replicates, the adherent biofilm-associated fraction consistently exhibited higher biomass-normalized crude VIO production than the corresponding suspended fraction, with 4.51-, 20.05-, and 5.51-fold increases. Although the adherent fraction represented only 10.6-24.0% of the total biomass, it contributed 35.4-86.3% of the total crude VIO. These results show that carrier-associated spatial organization within the partitioned bioreactor supported the formation of highly productive biofilm-associated E. coli co-culture populations. The presented concept highlights the potential of spatially organized, carrier-associated co-cultures for the intensification of secondary metabolite production and future biofilm-based bioprocessing applications.

works.title: Extraction, physicochemical, thermal, and rheological characterization of gelatin from milkfish (Chanos chanos) skin using different pretreatment and extraction methods
works.abstract: Abstract The study investigated the extraction and characterization of gelatin from milkfish skin ( Chanos chanos ) using different pretreatment and extraction methods. The effects of acetic acid, combined sulfuric acid-acetic acid pretreatments, ultrasound-assisted extraction, and optimized multi-step extraction were evaluated. Extraction conditions significantly affected gelatin yield and functional properties. The highest yield (42.63 ± 1.63%) was obtained using ultrasound-assisted extraction combined with sulfuric acid and acetic acid pretreatment. Ultrasound treatment also improved the thermal and rheological properties of gelatin, resulting in higher melting (33.30 °C) and gelling temperatures (19.70 °C). Gelatin produced using acetic acid pretreatment and ultrasound exhibited greater viscosity (11.92 cP) and gel strength (219.57 g) than gelatin obtained through conventional extraction methods. Color analysis showed ΔE* values ranging from 55.37 to 59.19, indicating retention of the natural gelatin pigmentation. Overall, ultrasound-assisted extraction combined with appropriate acid pretreatment enhanced gelatin yield and improved its physicochemical, thermal, and rheological characteristics.

works.title: Giving AI a seat at the peer review table
From off-target to on-demand: Precision engineering and translational evaluation of next-generation base editors
Bioengineering strategies for prenatal therapy
Morphology–Rheology Coupling Enables Predictive Optimization of Hirsutella sinensis Submerged Fermentation: A Case Study With Cross‐Strategy Predictive Modeling
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Hirsutella sinensis , the anamorph of Ophiocordyceps sinensis , is a valuable medicinal fungus, yet its industrial production is constrained by low fermentation efficiency and poorly controlled mycelial morphology. In this study, morphology engineering strategies based on inoculum volume and microparticle‐enhanced cultivation were systematically investigated to improve fermentation performance. Increasing inoculum volume (4%–10%, v/v) promoted a transition from dense (L‐type) to loose (S‐type) pellets, enhancing internal mass transfer and increasing biomass up to 18.7 g/L (compared to 11.1 g/L at 4% inoculum). Among the tested microparticles, talc exhibited the strongest effect, increasing biomass by 1.45‐fold compared to the control without microparticles and significantly enhancing adenosine and mannitol production. Microscopic and elemental analyses revealed that talc modifies pellet architecture via mechanical embedding and structural disruption, leading to increased internal porosity. Quantitative models linking morphology (S%, L%, density H) and rheology (Ln viscosity) to biomass achieved high predictive accuracy ( R 2 up to 0.92). Notably, a cross‐process model demonstrated that morphology descriptors can serve as predictive state variables across different engineering strategies. Scale‐up in a 5 L bioreactor further validated the approach, with a semi‐continuous process achieving 44.68 g/week productivity (compared to 25.93 g/week for batch fermentation, an 73% increase). This study establishes a morphology–rheology–performance framework for H. sinensis and provides a methodological insight applicable to other filamentous fermentation systems.

works.title: Distinction between Listeria species and L. monocytogenes serotypes with a handheld, VNIR hyperspectral imaging camera
works.abstract: Abstract A handheld, visible near-infrared (VNIR) hyperspectral imaging (HSI) camera was used to differentiate between Listeria species ( L. monocytogenes , L. ivanovii and L. innocua ) and two L. monocytogenes serotypes: 1/2a and 4b. The results indicated that portable HSI cameras could effectively be used for pathogen detection and distinction applications, despite lower spectral resolution and higher sensitivity to noise when compared to benchtop CCD-based instruments. Five hundred and fifty-five hyperspectral images were collected from pure cultures on agar plates throughout seven sampling campaigns. Sixty-five percent of samples/isolates ( n =± 90 samples per class) were used to train Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) models and 35% of samples ( n =± 50 samples per class) were used for validation. An overall classification accuracy (validation) of 74.5% was achieved for species-level discrimination through a four-class model ( L. monocytogenes 1/2a, L. monocytogenes 4b, L. ivanovii and L. innocua ), which demonstrates moderate performance within the VNIR range. However, Species-level performance was uneven across classes, with lower validation accuracies for L. innocua (68.0%) and L. ivanovii (63.0%) compared to L. monocytogenes 1/2a (71.8%) and 4b (95.2%). In contrast, a two-class model achieved ~ 90% accuracy for serotype-level discrimination between L. monocytogenes serotypes 1/2a and 4b. This highlights a novel use of portable VNIR cameras as a rapid, non-destructive serotyping aid. Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) score plots were used to characterise valuable wavelengths in the visible range that were significant for discriminant analysis, for example, 690 nm was significant for the classification of L. innocua , whilst 871 nm was associated with L. ivanovii. Notably, all the significant absorption regions used to differentiate between the L. monocytogenes serotypes were in the visible range (480–525 nm, 540–560 nm, 610 nm and 690 nm) despite the colony morphology being virtually identical for these organisms on brain heart infusion agar. Key points • A portable HSI camera was used to distinguish between Listeria colonies on agar • PLS-DA accuracy of 74.5% was obtained for classification between Listeria species • PLS-DA accuracy of 90% obtained for classification between L. monocytogenes serotypes

works.title: Dimyristoylphosphatidylcholine vesicle treatment enhances the storage stability and culturability of Lactococcus lactis suspensions
works.abstract: Abstract Maintaining bacterial culturability during storage is important for microbial biotechnology. This study evaluated dimyristoylphosphatidylcholine (DMPC) liposomes as a treatment for Lactococcus lactis suspensions stored for 28 days at 4 °C and room temperature. Liposomes were formed by thin-film hydration in the presence of bacterial cells. Cryogenic scanning electron microscopy (cryo-SEM) revealed approximately 100–160 nm vesicular structures in the DMPC-only sample and similar nanostructures near cells in treated suspensions, without establishing a continuous coating. On day 28 at 4 °C, treated and untreated suspensions had apparent zeta potentials of −17.31 and −1.56 mV, respectively. Across storage conditions and sampling times, polydispersity indices were 0.34–0.42 for treated suspensions versus 0.46–0.87 for controls, indicating lower apparent size heterogeneity. At room temperature on day 1, turbidity, expressed as optical density at 600 nm, was 0.99 versus 0.43, respectively. Metabolic activity assessed by 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)− 2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) reduction reached 2.50 versus 0.93 MTT-reducing units under the same conditions and subsequently declined, reaching 0.35 units in treated suspensions on day 14. Culturability was higher in treated suspensions from day 7 onward at both temperatures. On day 28 at room temperature, treated and untreated samples contained 2.55 × 10 5 and 3.83 × 10 1 CFU · mL −1 , respectively. DMPC liposome treatment thus supported retention of culturability during storage, with a larger relative benefit at room temperature, although the underlying vesicle-cell interactions remain unresolved. Key points • DMPC liposome treatment was associated with lower PDI in L. lactis suspensions. • DMPC treatment preserved L. lactis culturability during prolonged storage. • The protective effect of DMPC was strongest during room-temperature storage.

works.title: LysBM39 a novel T4-like lysozyme with antibiofilm activity against streptococcal pathogens associated with bovine mastitis
A Modular Micro‐Chemostat System for High‐Throughput Continuous Cultivations
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the fidelity of computational eukaryotic models will require an enormous amount of high quality and reproducible data from biological experiments. In this study we present and demonstrate a modular 12‐channel micro‐chemostat system. This micro‐chemostat is designed for use by Genesis, a Robot Scientist developed to automate scientific research in yeast systems biology. We performed bioreactor characterization experiments to evaluate the performance of the micro‐chemostat system. We also cultivated the Saccharomyces cerevisiae reference strain, BY4741, at three different dilution rates (0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 h −1 ) and under two aeration conditions (microaerobic and aerobic), resulting in six different conditions. The bioreactor performance fulfilled our requirements, and enabled substrate‐limited continuous cultivation of yeast. Furthermore, the empirical results from the biological experiments were consistent with the literature, suggesting that results obtained from our system are comparable to those reported for other platforms in the field. Based on the evidence presented in this study, we conclude that the 12‐channel micro‐chemostat system is a suitable platform for yeast systems biology research. The modular design of the micro‐chemostat system enables future scaling to hundreds or thousands of concurrent chemostats and facilitates integration with autonomous agents for automated optimization and improvement of eukaryotic model systems.

works.title: Bacterial-fungal cross-kingdom interactions in synthetic consortia: boosting secondary metabolites and sustainable food fermentation
works.abstract: Bacterial-fungal consortia (BFC) consistently outperform aseptic or single-species cultures in producing high-value secondary metabolites, yet the underlying cross-kingdom interaction mechanisms remain poorly understood. In food fermentations, BFCs enhance process robustness, substrate turnover, and bioactive profiles for sustainable functional foods. In these consortia, bacteria and fungi engage in complex cooperative and competitive interactions, involving signaling molecules, genetic regulation, and metabolic flux redistribution to enhance secondary metabolite yields. Based on the ecological compatibility and molecular communication mechanisms, a synthetic microbiology framework for constructing high-yield BFCs was proposed. This systematic approach included selecting appropriate coculture partners, setting up the BFC, and optimizing cultivation conditions. Functional BFCs can be effectively applied to: food fermentation, improving fermentation efficiency, nutritional value, flavor complexity, and food safety. The review provides an overview of BFCs for secondary metabolite production, with emphasis on their cross-kingdom communication mechanisms. It explores the construction and optimization of BFCs and their applications in food fermentation, identifying future directions for enhancing secondary metabolite yields.

works.title: Type III effector repertoires as a window into Pseudomonas syringae pv . actinidiae evolution and Actinidia defense responses
works.abstract: (Psa), represents a complex disease system in which closely related bacterial populations differ in host association, pathogenicity, genomic composition, and geographic distribution as evidenced by pandemic spread of biovar 3 after 2008. Closely related Psa lineages differ in host association, virulence, and distribution, yet these differences arise largely outside the conserved core genome. Mobile genetic elements remodel accessory regions, and acquisition, loss, and redundancy of type III effectors shape whether a lineage colonizes or is restricted by a given Actinidia genotype. Virulence is therefore a host-dependent property, not a fixed lineage rank. On the host side, genome assemblies, QTL mapping, and infection transcriptomics indicate that resistance reflects the timing and persistence of immune signalling rather than receptor presence alone, although few candidate receptors have been validated in planta. Durable resistance is most likely to derive from recognition of non-redundant effector functions and from immune hubs, such as RIN4, that multiple effectors target. Integrating pathogen population genomics, effector biology, and host immune genetics is the route to predicting which lineages will emerge next.

works.title: The historical evolution of CHO cell line development for biologics production: 60 years and still counting
works.abstract: Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells have played a central role in the production of therapeutic proteins since their initial isolation in the 1950s. Over the decades, scientific innovations have transformed CHO cells into the powerhouse of the biopharmaceutical industry. From rudimentary culture conditions and random integration of transgenes into the host genome, to synthetic biology, genetic engineering, high-performing chemically defined media, targeted transgene integration and AI-driven cell line development strategies, each decade has introduced transformative tools, knowledge, and insights to improve CHO cell line development and characterization processes. This review outlines the chronological history of the CHO cell line development process, decade by decade, highlighting central milestones and innovations, technological breakthroughs, and the role of key innovative steps that have enabled modern cell line development workflows and ultimately the industrial-scale manufacturing of biologics.

works.title: Sustainable biomanufacturing of rare ginsenosides from Panax notoginseng : a critical review
works.abstract: Rare ginsenosides (e.g. C-K, Rg3, Rh2) hold therapeutic promise but are severely constrained by low natural abundance. This review critically examines the entire biomanufacturing pipeline from green extraction to multi-modal conversion and de novo biosynthesis. Unlike previous reviews focusing on single technologies, this work systematically evaluates physical, chemical, and biological strategies and proposes an integrated upstream-midstream-downstream framework. Physical and chemical conversion methods can produce rare ginsenosides from abundant common precursors in Panax notoginseng, yet suffer from harsh conditions, poor selectivity, and C-20 epimeric mixtures. Biotransformation offers high regioselectivity, mild conditions, and retention of the desired 20(S)-configuration. However, distinct challenges exist such as microbial whole-cell fermentation suffers from complex metabolic networks, long cycles, and difficult separation, while enzymatic catalysis faces high enzyme costs, poor stability, and single-step limitations. Notably, while de novo biosynthesis draws upon key enzyme genes from Panax notoginseng to theoretically eliminate plant dependence, facing metabolic burden, low titers, and high costs, remain far from industrial viability. We highlight biocatalytic strengths including enzyme-mediated precise deglycosylation and recent breakthroughs in directed enzyme engineering for single products. From a techno-economic perspective, enzymatic conversion remains the most competitive route for producing rare ginsenosides at present, whereas de novo biosynthesis currently lacks the efficiency and economic feasibility to replace it.

works.title: From cell factories to photobiocatalysts: reengineering cyanobacteria for solar-driven chemical manufacturing
works.abstract: To achieve more sustainable, light-powered chemical manufacturing, cyanobacterial engineering is expanding from conventional carbon-accumulating “cell factories” toward the complementary use of cyanobacteria as “whole-cell photobiocatalysts.” This review critically examines this conceptual extension. By shifting the engineering focus from carbon-centric biosynthesis to electron- and energy-coupled catalysis, this emerging approach partially decouples target-product formation from the de novo assembly of CO2-derived carbon skeletons. Instead, it exploits photosynthetically generated reducing equivalents and ATP to support redox and energy-dependent enzymatic transformations, thereby reducing dependence on external cofactor- or energy-regeneration systems. We outline a multidimensional engineering framework that integrates carbon-flux redirection (“push”), coupling to photosynthetically generated reducing equivalents and ATP (“drive”), and product-removal-driven “pull” through secretion, volatilization, or in situ extraction. We further highlight advances in light-tolerant and stress-robust cyanobacterial chassis, together with emerging process strategies based on attached-growth and biofilm photobioreactors. We also critically consider genetic instability, variable enzyme-coupling efficiency, and scale-dependent light and mass-transfer limitations. Finally, we discuss the biophysical and energetic limits of light-to-chemical conversion, competition for reducing power, the largely conceptual potential of temporally decoupled light harvesting and dark-phase catalysis, and the need to select economically viable target products using rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle analyses. Collectively, this review provides conceptual and practical guidance for developing sustainable photosynthetic biomanufacturing platforms.

works.title: Biotechnological production of caffeoylquinic acids from plant cell and organ cultures for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic applications
works.abstract: Caffeoylquinic acids (CQAs) are phenolic compounds found in a wide variety of plants. These are a broad class of secondary metabolites that are primarily synthesized by esterifying quinic acids and hydroxycinnamic acids (ferulic acid, p-coumaric acid, and caffeic acid). The most common and significant of these in the human diet is chlorogenic acid, also known as 5-O-caffeoylquinic acid (5-CQA). In addition, plants have been found to contain mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra-esters. CQAs exhibit a wide range of biological activities, including anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer, neuroprotective, antiviral, antibacterial, antiparasitic, and antidiabetic effects. In addition to their dietary significance, CQAs are used extensively in pharmacology, animal husbandry, food preservation, and the manufacturing of skin care products. CQA accumulation varies greatly across several species, plant parts, and organs. As a result, in vitro cell and organ culture techniques have been used by researchers to produce CQAs. In a variety of plant species, callus, cells, adventitious/hairy roots, and plantlet cultures have been established. In these culture types, several techniques, including cell line selection, appropriate media, salt strength, plant growth regulators, chemical and physical variables, and elicitation, have been successfully assessed.

works.title: Targeted flavour development in chocolate: omics-driven insights into cocoa fermentation
works.abstract: Cocoa fermentation is the critical microbially driven process that transforms the genetic potential of cocoa beans into the complex flavour precursors essential for high-quality chocolate. Despite its importance, fermentation remains highly variable and poorly controlled, representing a major bottleneck in the production of premium chocolate. This review explores how advanced multi-omics approaches are improving our understanding of cocoa fermentation and flavour formation by linking microbial ecology, metabolite production and sensory outcomes. It highlights the transition of cocoa fermentation from a traditional practice towards a predictive, controllable biotechnological process. Such advances pave the way for the development of tailored starter cultures, optimised fermentation processes, and ultimately, consistent production of targeted flavour development in chocolates with enhanced quality and market value.

works.title: Chemical profiles, acaricidal activity, and enzymatic and transcriptomic mechanisms of Cinnamomum tamala essential oil and cinnamaldehyde against Hyalomma asiaticum
works.abstract: Abstract Hyalomma asiaticum , a Palearctic species of significant medical and veterinary relevance, has been identified as a primary vector for Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Q fever, spotted fever, Tick-borne Encephalitis, Theileriosis, and Anaplasmosis. This study evaluated the efficacy of Cinnamomum tamala EO in controlling ticks through transcriptomic analysis and enzymatic assays. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry revealed that cinnamaldehyde is the principal component of C. tamala EO. Larval packet tests demonstrated that C. tamala EO exhibited significant acaricidal activity against unfed larvae of H. asiaticum . Immersion tests indicated that both C. tamala EO and cinnamaldehyde displayed considerable acaricidal effects on unfed nymphs and adults of H. asiaticum . Enzymatic assays showed that cinnamaldehyde significantly inhibited carboxylesterase activity while enhancing acetylcholinesterase levels. This research focuses on short-term transcriptomic alterations analyzed via RNA sequencing in H. asiaticum following treatment with C. tamala EO, aiming to identify differentially expressed genes post-treatment with this essential oil. Notably, flavin monooxygenase was significantly upregulated after exposure to C. tamala EO; results from RT-qPCR corroborated those obtained from transcriptome sequencing analyses. These findings suggest that FMOs are implicated in the detoxification mechanisms employed by H. asiaticum in response to C. tamala EO treatment which may help mitigate the development of acaricide resistance among ticks, indicating that C. tamala EO could serve as an effective alternative to synthetic chemical acaricides.

works.title: Sequence-diversity-guided discovery, model-guided mutagenesis, and secretory production of GH5 endoglucanases in Bacillus subtilis
works.abstract: Cellulases are central to lignocellulose deconstruction, but identifying additional glycoside hydrolase family 5 (GH5) enzymes remains slow. Deep-learning predictors have proliferated, yet few studies carry their predictions through experimental validation and testing in a production host. A 23-gene panel was assembled by CatPred-based selection from clustered UniProt sequences (25,148 initial entries) and EglS-seeded homology-search results, supplemented by two comparative routes. Twenty-two candidates were assayed on carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) after expression in Escherichia coli , with EglS as a separate control. AQSP_CL and MACA_CL, for which we found no prior biochemical characterisation, were purified alongside EglS and the thermophilic benchmark Cel5A. Both new enzymes had short-assay optima of 70 °C. AQSP_CL was most active at pH 5.0 and gave an apparent mass-based CMC kinetic-efficiency estimate close to EglS (0.201 versus 0.231 U·mL·mg⁻2); Cel5A was more thermostable. CatPred cellotetraose predictions showed no detected correlation with lysate CMC activity in eight assayed candidates with reconciled identities ( ρ = 0.10, p = 0.82). AQSP_CL had the highest fraction of poses meeting the operational distance criterion in ensemble docking (52.0% versus 28.7–39.0%), although the differences were not resolved at the conformer level and Vina scores did not distinguish the enzymes. In first-round screening, M65Q had the highest measured lysate activity among single substitutions (1.61-fold wild type). A few-shot model trained on first-round data nominated the second-round library, but additive predictions did not generalise to combinations. Signal peptide SP3 increased extracellular activity of parental AQSP_CL in Bacillus subtilis approximately eightfold over the signal-peptide-free construct. The study links discovery of two GH5 endoglucanases to experimental assessment of computational nominations, lead-enzyme development and extracellular production. AQSP_CL provides a new scaffold for further biomass-deconstruction research. The CMC and flask-scale measurements establish enzyme properties and extracellular recovery; biomass-conversion performance remains to be evaluated.

works.title: High-throughput mass spectrometry-based metabolomics for large-scale population studies: technical barriers and recent innovations
works.abstract: Large-scale metabolomic studies are needed to identify and validate biomarkers for their successful translation in emerging population health and precision medicine initiatives. Yet, untargeted mass spectrometry (MS)-based metabolomics remains hampered by low sample throughput, limited coverage, complicated data processing, poor standardization, and high operating costs. These challenges also contribute to a reproducibility crisis, with most reported biomarkers not independently replicated, given variations in study designs, sample workup protocols, instrumental methods, and data pre-processing workflows. This review will focus on new advances in high-throughput MS platforms and computational software with emerging artificial intelligence/machine learning tools that are scalable, faster, and less prone to error. Recent progress to improve data harmonization in population-level metabolomic, lipidomic, and exposomic studies (n > 1000) will also be discussed. This will include strategies to correct for long-term batch effects, improve metabolite identification, and derive biochemical insights into disease mechanisms when integrated with multi-omic studies.

works.title: Editorial overview: Environmental Biotechnology in 2026: challenges, opportunities, and new frontiers
Comparative Modeling of Integrated Fixed‐Film Activated Sludge Membrane Bioreactor and Aerobic Membrane Bioreactor Systems: Nitrogen Dynamics and Energy Demand
works.abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a process‐oriented modeling assessment of a membrane bioreactor (MBR) and a hybrid integrated fixed‐film activated sludge membrane bioreactor (IFAS‐MBR) system using experimental data collected from parallel pilot‐scale systems, with emphasis on performance‐energy trade‐offs relevant to engineering design and operation. Both configurations were calibrated and validated under dynamic conditions to evaluate carbon removal, nitrogen transformation, and operational energy demand. Model results showed high predictive accuracy for mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) (mean relative absolute error, MRAE < 5%) and moderate accuracy for soluble chemical oxygen demand (sCOD) (MRAE: 11%–17%), while particulate COD (xCOD) predictions were governed primarily by membrane separation rather than biological kinetics. Nitrogen modeling revealed moderate agreement for ammonium nitrogen (NH 4 ‐N) (MRAE: 24%–36%), whereas nitrate nitrogen (NO 3 ‐N) predictions showed high accuracy, particularly in the IFAS‐MBR system (MRAE: 7%–14%). This improvement was achieved by calibrating oxygen diffusion within the biofilm, demonstrating that oxygen transport processes can dominate nitrogen transformation under non‐limiting bulk oxygen conditions. The IFAS‐MBR configuration increased total energy demand by approximately 27%, mainly due to intensified aeration requirements. These findings highlight the critical role of aeration in simultaneously governing process performance and energy demand.

works.title: Nitrogen ion beam mutagenesis improves sophorolipid production and properties in Starmerella bombicola
works.abstract: Abstract Sophorolipids (SLs) are microbial biosurfactants with broad industrial potential, but their large-scale application relies on robust high-producing strains with desirable functional properties.
