In this study, Starmerella bombicola CGMCC 1576 was subjected to nitrogen (N+) ion beam mutagenesis to improve SL production and product performance. A mutant library containing 124 isolates was constructed, and two stable high-producing mutants, 2–21 and 3–5, were obtained through high-throughput screening and shake-flask validation. Mutant 2–21 preferentially accumulated acidic sophorolipids (ASL) and showed the highest total sophorolipid (TSL) production, whereas mutant 3–5 produced more lactonic sophorolipids (LSL). HPLC profiling showed that the mutants retained the major SL components of the parental strain but differed markedly in component abundance and product distribution. Transcriptional analysis revealed upregulation of genes associated with fatty acid utilization, SL biosynthesis and metabolite transport, particularly in mutant 2–21 at 96 h, suggesting enhanced precursor conversion and product accumulation. Functional assays further showed composition-dependent differences in surface activity and mildness. LSL-rich fractions exhibited stronger surface activity, while ASL-rich fractions showed lower zein solubilization and hemolytic activity. In 100-L bioreactor fermentation, mutant 2–21 produced 224.31 g/L TSL, confirming its scalability and production robustness. These results demonstrate that N+ ion beam mutagenesis is an effective strategy for developing high-producing S. bombicola strains and tailoring SL composition for functional applications. Key points Nitrogen ion beam mutagenesis improved SL production in S. bombicola.ASL-rich and LSL-rich mutants showed distinct SL profiles.Mutant 2–21 produced 224.31 g/L TSL in a 100-L bioreactor.

works.title: Identification and functional characterization of RepE variants that increase plasmid copy number
works.abstract: Abstract Replication of low-copy-number iteron plasmids is tightly controlled by initiator proteins that coordinate replication initiation with transcriptional autoregulation. In the F-plasmid system, RepE fulfills both functions through a balance between monomeric and dimeric forms. Here, random mutagenesis of the repE gene combined with high-stringency selection was used to identify variants that modulate plasmid copy number. Two point mutations, A78S and Q45L, were identified and shown by qPCR and ddPCR to increase the copy number of plasmid pFO1 relative to the parental repE(R118P) allele. The mutations exhibited growth-phase-dependent effects, with A78S having a stronger impact during exponential growth and Q45L during stationary phase. A double mutant showed a cumulative effect, particularly in exponential phase. RepE transcription increased in the presence of pFO1 and correlated with plasmid copy number, supporting a titration-based regulatory model. These findings demonstrate that engineering RepE variants enables tunable control of plasmid copy number, offering a useful strategy for optimizing gene dosage in synthetic biology and biotechnological applications. Key points • RepE variants enable fi ne-tuning of plasmid copy number. • Gene dosage can be modulated without changing plasmid architecture. • RepE engineering off ers potential applications in biotechnology.

works.title: Dual-origin probiotic formulation attenuates intestinal inflammation in experimental colitis
works.abstract: Abstract Intestinal inflammation associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is driven by complex interactions between host immunity and gut microbiota, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional immunosuppressive drugs. In the present study, a dual-origin probiotic formulation comprising Lactobacillus plantarum AG40V (plant-derived) and Lactobacillus fermentum HO17HF (human-derived) was developed and evaluated for its safety and anti-inflammatory efficacy in a 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced colitis model in Sprague–Dawley rats. The formulation (1012 CFU/mL; 1:1 ratio) exhibited stability under refrigerated conditions and demonstrated significant in vitro functional antioxidant activities. Acute and sub-acute oral toxicity studies, conducted in accordance with OECD guidelines, confirmed the safety of the formulation, with no mortality or significant alterations in physiological, haematological, biochemical, or histopathological parameters. In the TNBS-induced colitis model, oral administration of the probiotic formulation resulted in marked attenuation of intestinal inflammation, as evidenced by reduced levels of nitric oxide, myeloperoxidase, and lipid peroxidation, along with enhanced catalase activity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the dual-origin probiotic formulation is safe and functionally effective in mitigating intestinal inflammation through modulation of oxidative stress and host inflammatory responses. This study highlights the translational potential of ecologically diverse probiotic consortia as a promising strategy for the management of inflammatory gastrointestinal disorders. Key points Dual-origin probiotics showed safety in experimental colitisTreatment reduced inflammation and improved gut healthFindings support probiotic potential in inflammatory bowel disease

works.title: Expanding the structural landscape of cytochrome P450 reductases and the effect of redox mediators on CYP-catalyzed reactions
works.abstract: Abstract Cytochrome P450 reductases (CPRs) are microsomal diflavin oxidoreductases that transfer electrons from nicotinamide cofactors to class II cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs). CPRs can also reduce other proteins, including cytochrome b 5 , heme oxygenase, and components of the fatty acid elongation system, as well as nonphysiological acceptors such as cytochrome c , ferricyanide, and various drugs. Although structural and functional studies have provided valuable insights into CPRs, the available data remain insufficient to fully elucidate their electron transfer mechanism and interactions with diverse redox partners. Here, we report the structural and functional characterization of two fungal CPRs from Candida albicans ( Cal CPR) and Mycosarcoma maydis (formerly Ustilago maydis , Uma CPR) and compare their properties with previously characterized CPRs. N -terminal truncation enabled soluble expression in Escherichia coli , and kinetic parameters were determined using cytochrome c and ferricyanide. Although Uma CPR shares greater sequence similarity with ascomycete CPRs than with mammalian CPRs, its overall structure displays features more closely resembling mammalian CPRs, including its FAD-binding topology. We further investigated the ability of both CPRs to support C. albicans CYP52A21 activity and evaluated the effects of reaction environment and redox mediators on CYP–CPR reconstitution. Both truncated CPRs supported CYP activity, with CPR performance strongly influenced by the reaction environment. Addition of the redox mediator cytochrome b 5 from M. maydis significantly enhanced product formation, including when a nonnative CPR was used. These findings highlight the structural diversity and functional plasticity of CPRs and demonstrate that the broader redox environment can strongly influence CYP–CPR efficiency, extending the complexity of electron transfer beyond the canonical CYP–CPR pairing. Key points • CPRs from ascomycetes and basidiomycetes fungi exhibit distinct structural features. • The CPR from Mycosarcoma (Ustilago) maydis is structurally more similar to mammalian CPRs. • CYP-CPR activity is strongly influenced by reaction environment and cytochrome b5 and extends beyond the canonical protein pairing.

works.title: Development of isopentenol utilization pathway based on cell-free metabolic engineering and its application in multienzyme cascades synthesis
The E. coli lite strains: New expression strains for the production of toxic membrane proteins
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The production of recombinant biopharmaceuticals is a billion-dollar industry, with numerous high-value proteins expressed in the bacterium Escherichia coli. Many recombinant protein production (RPP) systems enable the synthesis and purification of large amounts of soluble recombinant protein. However, such systems are often too strong to allow the expression of difficult-to-fold proteins, such as membrane proteins, with high-level RPP resulting in the production of insoluble aggregates ( i.e. , inclusion bodies), target protein degradation and even cell death. To aid the production of problematic proteins, we have engineered the E. coli lite strains in which the plasmid copy number regulator pcnB has been disrupted to allow expression levels of protein targets to be immediately lowered. Using the E. coli lite strains, we express a variety of proteins including green fluorescent protein (GFP), human growth hormone (hGH) and three toxic membrane proteins (BamA ENm , LetB EPEC and YiaM). We show that the E. coli lite strains are able to substantially lower the expression of target proteins and alleviate the cellular toxicity associated with producing membrane-localised proteins. Additionally, we show that the E. coli lite strains are extremely versatile, functioning with a variety of RPP systems, including lac- , T7 RNA polymerase- and paraBAD- based systems, and operate under different expression and growth regimes. Thus, the E. coli lite strains can be used to quickly lower expression levels of complicated target proteins to improve both protein production and cell growth.

works.title: Biosynthesis of 4-hydroxyvalerate from glycerol in engineered Pseudomonas putida KT2440 and its application for the production of poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate-co-4-hydroxy valerate) (P(3HB-co-3HV-co-4HV)) terpolymer
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The 4-hydroxyvalerate (4HV) is a key intermediate that serves as a precursor for γ-valerolactone (GVL) and terpolymers, contributing to the synthesis of liquid fuels and biodegradable plastics with improved properties. While 4HV is typically derived from levulinic acid (LA) via chemical catalysis, these methods are limited by high costs and operational complexity. In our previous study, we designed an engineered Pseudomonas putida KT2440 with double knockout of pcaIJ and lvaR and introduction of aroG , asbF , and adc , enabling high production of LA from glycerol. Herein, we introduced acyl-CoA synthetase gene ( lvaE ) and 4-hydroxyvaleryl-CoA dehydratase gene ( lvaD ) into LA producing strain to construct a 4HV production pathway from glycerol. The strain harboring both lvaD and lvaE consumed the highest amount of LA, and, subsequently, showed the highest 4HV production. In fed batch fermentation , P. putida KT2440 HP403 produced 28.77 mM of 4HV from glycerol. To expand its potential applications as a PHA precursor, biologically synthesized 4HV was supplied to the high-performing PHA producer Cupriavidus necator PHB -4 / phaC BP-M-CPF4 for polymer synthesis. This produced a terpolymer with the composition P(54.49 mol% 3HB- co -6.98 mol% 3HV- co -38.53 mol% 4HV) with a PHA content of 60.21%. The terpolymer exhibited improved elongation at break and lower glass transition and crystallization temperatures due to increased amorphicity. This study suggests a 4HV bioconversion strategy derived from glycerol by engineered P. putida KT2440 HP403 and demonstrates the production of a high-content P(3HB- co -3HV- co -4HV) terpolymer in C. necator containing high-mole fraction of 4HV, thereby providing a new sustainable approach for PHA production.

works.title: Preparation and characterization of SPF porcine decellularized tendon biomaterials
works.abstract: Tendon, a dense connective tissue linking bone and skeletal muscle, is decellularized to generate tendon-derived Extracellular Matrix (dECM) – an increasingly utilized biomaterial for tendon repair. This study employed specific pathogen-free (SPF) Rongchang porcine tendons to optimize decellularization methodology. Decellularization efficacy was quantified through histological analysis and residual dsDNA quantification, while proteomic composition was compared across anatomical regions and developmental stages. A decellularized tendon matrix membrane (DTM) was subsequently fabricated. In vitro biocompatibility assessment confirmed that DTM does not induce severe erythrocyte hemolysis, exhibits no potential cytotoxicity, and shows significant upregulation of the tendon-specific markers Scx and Tnmd , while Col1α1 and Tnc remain unchanged. In vivo subcutaneous implantation revealed no gross rejection phenotype. These findings establish an optimized decellularization protocol and provide essential biomaterial characterization data for porcine tendon dECM development, offering critical insights for donor selection and clinical translation of tendon repair strategies.

works.title: Valorization of non-recyclable polypropylene manufacturing waste via catalytic co-hydrothermal liquefaction with biomass using industrial alumina–silica waste as a heterogeneous catalyst
works.abstract: Non-recyclable polypropylene (PP) manufacturing waste and lignocellulosic/algal biomass residues represent two underutilized waste streams that are commonly disposed of by landfill or incineration. This study investigated the co-hydrothermal liquefaction (co-HTL) of sawdust, rice straw, and Chlorella with non-recyclable PP manufacturing waste under subcritical water conditions (350 °C), using industrial alumina–silica waste recovered from liquid nitrogen processing as a low-cost heterogeneous catalyst. The catalyst was characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), FTIR spectroscopy, and N 2 physisorption. Product distribution, elemental composition, higher heating value (HHV), Van Krevelen analysis, and FTIR spectroscopy were evaluated to determine the influence of catalyst addition on product quality. A screening-level environmental assessment was also performed to compare the estimated embodied carbon footprint of the waste-derived catalyst with reported values for synthetic and bio-derived zeolite catalysts. Catalyst addition increased the maximum bio-crude yield to 47.2 wt.% for the Chlorella–PP blend, while reducing the solid residue from 46.7 wt.% to 37.3 wt.%. The catalyst was mesoporous, with a BET surface area of 226.6 m 2 g −1 and an average pore diameter of 5.3 nm. Co-processing with PP substantially improved fuel characteristics, with the highest HHV reaching 32.95 MJ kg⁻ 1 and the O/C atomic ratio decreasing from 0.43 to 0.19, indicating enhanced deoxygenation and improved energy density. FTIR and Van Krevelen analyses were consistent with increased hydrocarbon formation and reduced oxygenated functional groups following catalytic treatment. The observed improvements are proposed to arise from catalyst-assisted cracking of polypropylene together with enhanced interactions between PP-derived hydrocarbons and biomass-derived intermediates during co-liquefaction. The waste-derived catalyst exhibited an estimated embodied carbon footprint of approximately 0.13 kg CO₂-eq kg⁻ 1 , which is substantially lower than values reported for conventional synthetic and bio-derived zeolite catalysts. These results demonstrate that industrial alumina–silica waste can serve as an effective low-cost heterogeneous catalyst for upgrading bio-crude during co-hydrothermal liquefaction, while simultaneously valorizing two problematic industrial waste streams. Further investigation of catalyst stability, aqueous-phase composition, long-term catalyst reusability, and comprehensive life cycle and techno-economic assessment is required before scale-up.
