Nuclease‐Free Scalable Purification of Physalis Mottle Virus‐Like Particles Expressed in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Plant virus-like particles (VLPs) are promising nanotechnology platforms, but their translation requires purification strategies suitable for large-scale production. Here, we developed a nuclease-free downstream process for Physalis mottle virus (PhMV) VLPs expressed in Escherichia coli, combining ammonium sulfate precipitation, low-pH extraction, ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF), and flow-through anion-exchange (AEX) chromatography. Ammonium sulfate precipitation separated the VLPs from bulk host nucleic acids, whereas extraction at low pH removed most host cell proteins (HCPs) while retaining the VLPs in solution. Subsequent UF/DF was used to concentrate VLPs and simultaneously achieve buffer exchange for downstream AEX chromatography, which removed remaining HCPs while the PhMV VLPs were collected in the flow-through fraction. This combined workflow produced PhMV VLPs with > 95% purity and a recovery of ~68%. Compared with conventional workflows based on ultracentrifugation and size-exclusion chromatography, the new process reduced the purification time from ~3 days to 1 day and hands-on processing time from ~18 h to 8 h, also increasing the average yield from ~80 to ~130 mg PhMV VLPs per liter of culture. The resulting particles were intact and monodisperse, with a lower content of encapsulated host nucleic acid than VLPs purified by ultracentrifugation. The VLPs also had increased chemical addressability of lysine and cysteine residues. These results establish a scale-up compatible, nuclease-free purification strategy for PhMV VLPs expressed in bacteria and provide a framework for the downstream processing of plant VLP platforms produced in microbial systems.

works.title: A Hybrid Mechanistic Model Capturing Lactate Run‐Away and Back‐Metabolism in Mammalian Cell Culture
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanistic modeling is important in biopharmaceutical manufacturing by enabling in‐silico experimentation. However, developing a robust mechanistic model for mammalian cell culture remains challenging due to the complexity of the underlying bioprocesses. Existing data‐driven models often suffer from limited extrapolation capability and require extensive datasets. Not all modeling approaches can accurately represent differing metabolic scenarios such as lactate consumption and production. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid mechanistic model for mammalian cell culture to improve predictive accuracy and process understanding. Our model integrates high‐frequency pH data with low‐frequency measurements of viable cell density (VCD), glucose, lactate, monoclonal antibody (mAb) concentrations from 10 runs (7 L). Novel kinetic equations for cell growth and death, and lactate metabolism considering both scenarios were developed. Additionally, our model enables automatic lactate switch detection based on time‐series pH and feeding data. It demonstrated high predictive capability with a mean R 2 of 0.88 for VCD, mAb, glucose, and lactate concentrations across training runs. Real‐time fine‐tuning further improved accuracy, reducing the root mean squared error (RMSE) for glucose by ~50% and for lactate by ~30%. The results indicate that our model provides accurate real‐time predictions of VCD, mAb, glucose, and lactate concentrations under variable bioprocessing conditions.

works.title: Serotype‐Tailored Midstream and Downstream Operations to Advance the Manufacturing of Adeno‐Associated Viral Vectors
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Adeno‐associated viruses (AAVs) are the leading vectors for in vivo gene therapy, fueling a growing demand for scalable and robust biomanufacturing processes. Yet, the impact of cell lysis conditions on the performance of midstream and downstream unit operations across serotypes remains poorly characterized. This study presents a serotype‐resolved investigation of cell lysis and its cascading effects on AAV2, AAV5, AAV8, and AAV9 processing. A panel of lysis methods including inorganic agents, non‐ionic and ionic detergents, and mechanical disruption was evaluated using an analytical framework of at‐ and off‐line assays to quantify AAV yield, purity, and activity at each stage. Our results reveal pronounced serotype‐specific differences: cetrimonium bromide (CTAB) delivered the highest transduction output of any condition evaluated for AAV8 (2.25 × 10 9 TU/mL) at 55.0% capture step yield, while sodium deoxycholate achieved ~ 98% host cell protein (HCP) reduction for AAV9 (HCP log reduction value 1.60) and the highest functional enrichment for AAV5 (6.73‐fold) and AAV8 (5.80‐fold). AAV2 proved uniquely challenging, with CTAB enabling the highest tangential flow filtration (TFF) yield. Acid precipitation paired with high salt addition reduced aggregation and improved permeate flux for AAV5 and AAV9. TFF performance was governed by the detergents' physicochemical properties: micelle‐forming agents generated multicomponent complexes that fouled membranes in condition‐ and serotype‐specific patterns. Rheological characterization revealed that all clarified lysates converged to the viscosity of the media after filtration, supporting transferable TFF parameters. Mixed‐mode chromatography using a peptide‐functionalized resin amplified lysis‐imprinted differences, decoupling step yield from functional enrichment. Bayesian optimization of the chromatographic step improved purification outcomes: for AAV8 residual HCPs in the eluate decreased > 300‐fold, from 0.91 mg/mL to 3 μg/mL, while for AAV9 the yield rose to ~95% at residual HCP as low as 14 μg/mL, demonstrating that purity and recovery are co‐optimizable when lysis, midstream, and downstream conditions are rationally paired.

works.title: Evaluating assay performance and freeze-thaw stability in cerebrospinal fluid samples using High-Throughput Proximity Extension Assay Platform
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) facilitates the understanding of brain-specific molecular changes that may associate with disease progression. Proximity extension assays (PEA) have been deployed in several CSF studies, however the evaluation of the assay and impact of freeze-thaw cycles on the protein signal has not been documented. We sought to (1) assess the technical performance of the PEA platform and (2) evaluate the effect of freeze-thaw cycles on the detectability of analytes on the PEA platform. RESULTS: We have evaluated the PEA with Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) readout assay and report on the detectability and coefficient of variation observed in CSF samples. We have also evaluated proteomic signals with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 9 freeze thaw cycles and detected very minimal change in signal with increasing cycle number. CONCLUSION: Our study is the first to evaluate the performance of PEA using NGS readout platform with CSF samples. We report lower protein detection rates and higher variability in the expansion panels compared to the original 4 panels, with acceptable variation above detectability threshold. In addition, our work demonstrates that the proteomic signal is robust and continues to be stable across multiple freeze thaw cycles. This is highly impactful to the processing and analysis of clinical samples and facilitates the investigation of samples with variable pre-analytical conditions.

works.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
works.abstract: Abstract Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf . In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf , Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet ; CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

works.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
works.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

works.title: Translating Innovation to Clinic: End‐to‐End Bioprocess Development and cGMP Manufacturing of N332‐GT5 HIV Vaccine Candidate for First‐In‐Human Trials (HVTN144)
works.abstract: The successful translation of rationally designed HIV-1 immunogens into effective vaccines requires manufacturing platforms that maintain structural conformity while meeting clinical-grade quality standards. We developed and scaled up a robust, cGMP-compliant process for N332-GT5 gp140, a germline-targeting envelope trimer designed to initiate broadly neutralizing antibody responses, which is now undergoing first-in-human evaluation in HVTN144. Starting with a stable CHO cell line developed using Leap-In® transposon technology, we established a production clone exhibiting high-titer expression (> 200 mg/L) and genetic stability through 60 population doublings. The manufacturing process scaled up efficiently from Ambr® 250 miniature bioreactors to 200-L single-use systems, delivering consistent product quality across multiple cGMP batches. A streamlined three-step purification strategy-affinity capture, multimodal polishing, and viral clearance -yielded > 99% trimeric purity while preserving quaternary structure and native-like antigenicity. Orthogonal LC-MS analyses confirmed site-specific glycan occupancy matching design specifications, while robust viral clearance exceeded 18-log and 11-log reductions for model retroviruses. Clinical material manufactured through this platform has been successfully administered in clinical trial HVTN144. This work establishes a scalable, reproducible manufacturing paradigm for structurally complex HIV-1 envelope immunogens, advancing the field toward rational vaccine design based on germline-targeting principles.

works.title: Amyloid‐Based Hydrogels as Emerging Biomaterials for Wound Healing: A Review
works.abstract: Wound healing is a complex and dynamic biological process that occurs in a series of coordinated steps, including hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, and tissue remodeling. Traditional wound dressings, such as gauze and bandages, are not suitable for healing because they do not maintain moisture levels and cannot prevent infections. So, hydrogels have been recognized as advanced wound-healing materials because of their high-water content and their ability to mimic the natural ECM. Additionally, amyloid-based hydrogels have been recognized for their unique physicochemical and functional properties, which are constructed by the self-assembly of peptides into highly ordered fibrillar structures. The nanoscale fibrillar structure provides the hydrogels with high mechanical stability and viscoelasticity. The porous structure allows the movement of oxygen and nutrients, as well as the removal of waste products. They can also self-heal and be formulated in injectable forms for application to wounds with irregular surfaces. Their unique structural and functional properties make them highly effective at accelerating wound healing. This review highlights in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrating the efficacy of amyloid-based hydrogels in accelerating wound healing, making them highly promising materials for advanced wound healing.

works.title: Induction Temperature and Feeding Profile Shape the Partitioning Between Soluble Product and Inclusion Body Formation in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Inclusion body (IB) processes yielding the recombinant product only as IBs are long-established in the biopharmaceutical industry. Yet, for recombinant proteins that accumulate both IBs and soluble fraction depending on the selected upstream processing (USP) strategy, the influence of process parameters on the partitioning between both forms remains poorly characterized. In this study, l-lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was selected as a model protein as it yields IBs and soluble protein concurrently. We investigated how induction temperature and specific substrate uptake rate shift the relative amount of soluble product. A response surface model revealed a sharp switch between exclusively soluble production at 25°C, exclusive IB formation at 35°C and a mixed production regime at 30°C. Further, we investigated whether these trends hold for the structurally related proteins xylose isomerase (Xiso) and pyranose-2-oxidase (P2O) using a reduced diagonal design and a projection into the LDH latent space by principal component analysis (PCA). Results revealed that the shared structural features were not sufficient to predict the expression form. Still, the LDH model served as a reference framework for identifying the extent to which other mixed producers follow established process-response trends.

works.title: Editorial Board
Increasing diosmin production in a suspension culture of Scrophularia striata Boiss. Using fungal extracts in a bioreactor
works.abstract: Diosmin is a flavonoid glycoside renowned for its potent antioxidant, anti-hypertensive, anti-inflammatory, and anti-cancer properties. However, its natural abundance is limited, necessitating efficient production strategies. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the efficacy of Piriformospora indica mycelium extract as a biotic elicitor to enhance the biosynthesis of diosmin and other polyphenolic compounds in Scrophularia striata cell suspension cultures, comparing the efficiency of shake-flask and bioreactor systems. P. indica mycelium extract (250 mg l − 1 ) was applied at concentrations of 0, 0.5, 1, and 2% to 10-day-old cell cultures and the cells were harvested on 15th d. The optimal concentration was subsequently utilized for elicitation in bioreactor to assess the scalability of the production. Elicitation significantly modulated the metabolic profile of S. striata . In the bioreactor system, the 1% (v/v) extract treatment led to a significant 3.03-fold increase in diosmin accumulation compared to the control. Furthermore, the diosmin yield in the bioreactor was approximately 77-fold higher than that observed in shake-flask cultures. Other flavonoids and stilbenoids, such as resveratrol, also showed increased accumulation, although a reduction in total biomass was observed in response to the elicitor. These findings demonstrate that P. indica mycelium extract is a potent elicitor for the enrichment of diosmin in S. striata . The bioreactor system provided a significantly higher diosmin yield compared to shake-flask cultures under the tested conditions, suggesting its potential for further development in the production of this high-value compound.

works.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
works.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization. Human Argonaute is repurposed for RNA editing.

works.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity
works.abstract: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

works.title: Multienzyme cascades for non-grain carbon feedstocks valorization: Recent advances and perspectives
Structurally informed metabolite measurements with ion mobility-mass spectrometry
works.abstract: Although ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS) is no longer a new technology, new developments in instrumentation and resources for structurally informed measurements are enabling the use of IM-MS in emerging metabolomic applications. Once limited by experimental measurements, the growth of machine-learning strategies to predict collision cross-section values is rapidly increasing the coverage of IM-MS information in metabolite databases. IM-MS instrumentation capable of high-resolution separations is bringing new depth to the level of structural annotation that can be achieved, while creative strategies to combine IM-MS with complementary analytical or chemical methods are further leveraging its ability to resolve small molecule isomers and isobars. This brief review highlights the recent developments of IM-MS for metabolomics with a focus on applications to mass spectrometry imaging, rapid multi-omics, and single-cell analyses.

works.title: Engineering sticky microbes: A framework for appraisal of microbial cell-cell adhesion
works.abstract: Engineering bacterial consortia is key in biotechnological applications where specific spatial interactions among their components determine system performance. Genetic tools for programming cell-cell binding such as the nanobody-antigen (Nb-Ag; relying on non-covalent binding) and SpyCatcher-SpyTag (Spy; based on covalent linkage) systems are increasingly adopted as assets for enabling specific interactions of interest among otherwise detached members of a given combination of strains or species. Yet, despite the potential of these technologies, a robust metrology to quantify and compare the efficacy, stability, and specificity of inter-cell binding in a consortium is lacking. This work introduces a conceptual and experimental framework to systematically evaluate synthetic binding systems by combining aggregation assays, flow cytometry, and microscopy. Together, these techniques provide detailed insights into the structure and composition of engineered bacterial aggregates. This methodology was benchmarked with two Escherichia coli strains tagged with different fluorescent markers and engineered to surface-display matching adhesins. Under the test conditions, results showed that the Spy system outperformed the Nb-Ag system in terms of aggregation speed and stability. We also applied the same metrics for assessing the efficacy of the Spy system to mediate synthetic consortia of the opportunistic pathogenic bacterium Enterobacter cloacae. The robustness of the results suggests that the proposed framework could become a valuable tool for quantitative studies on designer bacterial consortia.

works.title: Host physiological constraints limit microbial production of partially acetylated chitooligosaccharides
works.abstract: Chitooligosaccharides (COS) are versatile biomolecules with applications across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic industries. Expanding the COS portfolio, particularly with partially acetylated COS (paCOS) possessing defined structural characteristics, including degree of deacetylation and pattern of acetylation, is essential for advancing structure-function studies and enabling tailored applications. This study investigates the heterologous co-expression of chitin deacetylases (CDAs) with a chitin oligosaccharide synthase (oCS) RhNodC in Escherichia coli for the in vivo production of paCOS. Although this approach enables paCOS formation, co-expression of NodC and CDAs results in reduced COS yields and incomplete conversion of fully acetylated COS into paCOS. To identify potential cellular bottlenecks underlying these limitations, stress responses were monitored using a stress promoter-based fluorescent reporter system. CDA co-expression activated protein quality control and membrane-associated stress responses. Furthermore, confocal microscopy revealed altered intracellular localization of both RhNodC and CDAs compared to individual expression, with enzymes detected in the cytoplasm, membrane and inclusion bodies. Co-expression also resulted in pronounced cellular elongation, further indicating cellular stress during pathway implementation. Together, these findings reveal cellular bottlenecks associated with enzyme co-expression and highlight the need for deeper exploration of RhNodC-CDA co-expression and approaches to mitigate cellular stress to improve in vivo paCOS production.

works.title: Editor’s pick: Bioptimus
Rumen microbiome carbohydrate metabolism is associated with host lipid metabolic differences between Wagyu and Nanyang cattle
works.abstract: Abstract The rumen microbiome plays an important role in converting dietary carbohydrates into metabolites associated with host physiology, yet the relationships between microbial carbohydrate metabolism and host lipid metabolism remain incompletely understood. Here, we compared Japanese Wagyu and Nanyang cattle to investigate microbiota–metabolite–host associations in relation to breed-associated differences in intramuscular fat (IMF) deposition. Metagenomic analysis revealed differences in rumen microbial community composition and functional profiles between breeds, including differential abundances of carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) families associated with polysaccharide degradation. Wagyu cattle exhibited higher abundances of glycoside hydrolase (GH) families GH5 (cellulose degradation) and GH92 (alpha-mannan degradation), whereas GH13 (starch degradation) and GH43 (arabinoxylan and arabinan degradation) were enriched in Nanyang cattle, together with differences in carbohydrate-degrading genera, including Prevotella , Fibrobacter , and Butyrivibrio . These microbial functional differences were accompanied by distinct fermentation profiles, with higher ruminal acetate and butyrate concentrations in Wagyu cattle and higher propionate concentrations in Nanyang cattle. Proteomic analysis of the longissimus dorsi muscle identified breed-associated differences in proteins involved in lipid synthesis, lipid storage, and energy metabolism, including FABP4, FASN, PLIN1, ACSS2, and IDH1, which showed higher abundances in Wagyu cattle. Correlation analyses identified associations among microbial taxa, CAZyme families, fermentation metabolites, and host proteins related to lipid metabolism and IMF deposition. Overall, these findings reveal coordinated breed-associated differences in rumen microbial functions, fermentation characteristics, and host lipid metabolic profiles, providing insights into microbiota–host metabolic associations related to IMF deposition in cattle. Keypoints • Rumen carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) profiles differ between Wagyu and Nanyang cattle. • Wagyu cattle show higher acetate and butyrate levels. • Microbiota–volatile fatty acids (VFAs)–proteome axis is linked to intramuscular fat (IMF) deposition

works.title: Numerical analysis of shear rate in a rocking bioreactor and its impact on HL-60 lymphocytes
works.abstract: Abstract The aim of the study was to investigate the influence of hydrodynamic parameters on HL-60 lymphocyte cultures in a rocking disposable bioreactor. A 2D CFD-based model employing the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method was used to characterize the culture microenvironment, while a rotational rheometer was used to determine critical shear thresholds. The developed numerical model was validated against experimental mixing times, yielding an absolute mean percentage difference of 29.2%, demonstrating high predictive accuracy at very low and very high Reynolds numbers, though limitations were observed at medium Reynolds numbers. Results indicated that while averaged shear rates remained below 22.5 s⁻1, local maximum shear rates significantly exceeded the lethal threshold of 1500 s⁻1 for all studied rocking conditions, reaching over 30 000 s⁻1 at the highest parameters. Analysis of shear rate effects on HL-60 lymphocytes demonstrated that cell viability decreases at shear rates higher than 1000 s⁻1 due to cell membrane disruption, up to total disintegration of cells above 1500 s⁻1. The consistent exceeding of these lethal thresholds, particularly during intensified rocking, was shown to negatively impact cell growth and increase the release of intracellular enzymes. Consequently, the successful application of rocking disposable bioreactors for shear-sensitive cultures requires a strategic trade-off between mixing intensification and the mitigation of lethal local shear effects. The developed computational model provides a valuable framework for such optimization and subsequent bioprocess scale-up. Keypoints • 2D CFD VOF model well predicts hydrodynamics in rocking bioreactors. • Local maximum shear rates exceed 1500 s−1 as lethal threshold for HL-60 cells. • Intensification of cell culture requires balanced mixing and hydrodynamic stress.

works.title: Programmable bacterial vaccine vectors: A Design–Build–Control framework for precision immune engineering
Feasibility Assessment of a Single‐pH Connected Polishing Train for Monoclonal Antibody Purification Using Mildly Acidic Protein A Elution and an Acidic‐Window Anion Exchange Membrane
works.abstract: Monoclonal antibody downstream processing often requires multiple pH adjustments between Protein A capture and polishing steps. These adjustments increase process complexity and make direct unit-operation connection more difficult. We evaluated a connected post-capture polishing block operated at approximately pH 5.0 using mild-pH Protein A elution, an acidic-window anion exchange (AEX) membrane, and cation exchange (CEX) chromatography. Praesto Jetted A50 HipH generated IgG1 eluates near pH 5.0 with conductivity suitable for direct AEX loading. Under standard condition (pH 5.0, 5.0 mS/cm), the AEX membrane reduced xenotropic murine leukemia virus to the assay limit (≥ 3 log10) and minute virus of mice by approximately 2-3 log10. In a connected proof-of-concept run without intermediate pH adjustment, the AEX-CEX polishing block reduced host cell proteins from > 25 to < 10 ng/mg-IgG and high-molecular-weight species from 1.3% to < 1% in the final product pool, maintained low-molecular-weight species below 1%, and achieved 97.6% product recovery. For two additional IgGs, archived strong-AEX flow-through records at pH 7.5 and sequence-derived charge descriptors supported the plausibility of product flow-through at pH 5.0. In a same-IgG1 retrospective comparison, the connected configuration used fewer vessels and conditioning operations and had shorter recipe-derived programmed chromatography time. These findings support process-representative evaluation of single-pH connected polishing.

works.title: Biogenic Magnetic Nanoplatform for Dual Tumor Microenvironment‐Responsive Aripiprazole Delivery in Breast Cancer
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Breast cancer remains a major global health challenge, highlighting the need for targeted drug delivery systems with improved therapeutic efficacy and reduced systemic toxicity. In this study, a green‐synthesized dual‐responsive magnetic nanoplatform, Iron oxide@Tween 80‐PEG‐ARI‐NPs, was developed for targeted breast cancer therapy. Iron oxide nanoparticles were synthesized using Nephelium lappaceum ( Rambutan ) peel extract as an eco‐friendly reducing and stabilizing agent, followed by functionalization with Tween 80, polyethylene glycol (PEG), and aripiprazole (ARI) loading. Comprehensive characterization using FTIR, XRD, SEM‐EDX, HR‐TEM, DLS, TGA/DTA, and VSM confirmed successful surface modification, spherical morphology, preserved crystallinity, superparamagnetic behavior, and enhanced colloidal stability. In vitro drug release studies demonstrated minimal ARI leakage at physiological pH 7.4 and accelerated release under acidic pH 5.5 and oxidative conditions, reaching 70.40% ± 0.55% and 90.35% ± 5.15% cumulative release after 60 h, respectively. Release kinetics followed anomalous non‐Fickian diffusion under acidic conditions and quasi‐Fickian diffusion at physiological pH. The nanoparticles exhibited significant anti‐inflammatory activity and potent cytotoxicity against MCF‐7 breast cancer cells, with an IC 50 of 40.2 ± 2.15 µg/mL, inducing pronounced apoptotic morphological changes. These findings demonstrate the potential of Iron oxide@Tween 80‐PEG‐ARI‐NPs as an effective dual‐responsive magnetic nanocarrier for targeted breast cancer therapy with enhanced therapeutic potential.

works.title: Engineering 4‐Vinylcatechol Biosynthesis in Escherichia coli Through Host–Enzyme Combination
works.abstract: De novo biosynthesis of 4-vinylcatechol (VCAT), a valuable bio-based monomer and potent antioxidant, has emerged as a crucial objective due to its profound industrial and pharmacological significance. However, its biosynthesis is frequently hindered by limited precursor availability. In this study, we developed a highly efficient, dual-plasmid platform utilizing engineered Escherichia coli cell factories to synthesize VCAT directly from glucose without precursor feeding. To establish optimal production cells, we evaluated combinations of different host strains and phenolic acid decarboxylase (PAD) sources. Our results indicate that BL21(DE3) is less suitable for efficient de novo VCAT biosynthesis under the conditions tested. In contrast, the rpoA14(DE3), featuring a reprogrammed shikimate pathway, provided a more favorable host for VCAT production and enabled endogenous tyrosine supply, thereby eliminating the need for exogenous tyrosine supplementation required in BL21(DE3). To maximize this enhanced intracellular flux, we comparatively evaluated padC genes from different Bacillus subtilis strains. Comparative analysis demonstrated that the rpoA14(DE3)-10A5 exhibited significantly superior production titers, markedly outperforming both its 168-PAD counterpart and the standard BL21(DE3) expression hosts. Cultivated in single-step, aqueous fermentation at mild conditions, this optimal host-enzyme combination achieved de novo accumulation of 200 mg/L VCAT, promising scalable biosynthesis.

works.title: Scalable production of highly enriched chitobiose shows promise in agriculture, promoting plant growth and bolstering immunity
works.abstract: Abstract Chitobiose is a high-value, chitin-derived disaccharide with promising potential for agricultural application. Unfortunately, current production methods rely on hazardous chemical and costly enzymatic processing and the resulting high cost prohibits its commercial application. In this work, we report a simple, scalable fermentation platform, based on a Streptomyces venezuelae ΔdasBC transporter mutant that converts raw chitin directly into chitobiose. By tuning production parameters to maximize titer, the process yielded an estimated ~ 450 mg/L chitobiose without chitin pretreatment or enzymatic steps. Liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry showed the product to be highly enriched for chitobiose with the absence of detectable longer N-acetylglucosamine oligomers. To explore the potential agricultural application, we tested the crude spent medium as a biostimulant. As a soil additive, it increased Arabidopsis thaliana rosette size by up to 22% and induced beneficial changes to root development, while foliar pretreatment decreased Botrytis cinerea infection symptoms and increased the immunity-related responses to fungal elicitors. Notably, this immune-priming activity surpassed that of a commercially available chitin oligomer mix at an equivalent mass concentration, highlighting its potency. Together, this work establishes a cost-effective microbial platform for the production of highly enriched chitobiose and demonstrates its utility as a bioproduct that promotes plant growth and defense. The approach enables sustainable valorization of chitin waste streams into a defined, bioactive molecule for agriculture applications.

works.title: From oleaginous microalga to marine chassis: synthetic biology and process-aware biomanufacturing in Nannochloropsis
Next-generation nano-biocatalysts: extremozyme-based nanoparticle system for cypermethrin bioremediation
works.abstract: Abstract Extremozymes, with their exceptional catalytic activity and stability under extreme environmental conditions, have great potential for pesticide remediation. This study involves the isolation and screening of a new extremozyme-producing microbe, Proteus mirabilis JB1, for the production of alkaline-pH-stable laccase. A primary OFAT screening tested a broad range of carbon sources (glucose, lactose, xylose, sucrose, starch, glycerol, cellulose, trisodium citrate, sodium acetate), nitrogen sources (ammonium sulfate, sodium nitrate, urea, beef extract, peptone, casein, gelatin), salts (0.1 mM and 0.01 mM) such as CuSO₄, KCl, ZnCl₂, MgCl₂, MnCl₂, NiCl₂, NaCl, and CaCl₂, and pH levels (7–10). The highest enzyme activity of 0.999 U/ml was achieved using 0.25% (w/v) cellulose, 0.8% (w/v) urea, 0.1 mM MnCl 2 , MgSO 4 , CaCl 2 , NaCl, and KCl, and 0.01 mM CuSO 4 , FeSO 4 , and NiCl 2 at pH 9 with good stability to surfactants (Tween 80, SDS), organic solvents (acetone, ethanol, methanol), and inhibitors (EDTA). PBD and CCD were then implemented to screen and optimize critical parameters—cellulose (1.5% w/v), urea (0.7% w/v), and MgSO₄ (0.05 mM)—to achieve an efficient increase in enzyme activity to 2.3 U/mL, demonstrating the strength and efficacy of the optimization process. Biogenic selenium nanoparticles (Bio-SeNPs) were fabricated and exhibited very high efficiency in pesticide degradation, achieving 100% degradation of cypermethrin without forming any toxic intermediates within 72 h. This research has provided a comprehensive and replicable technique covering microbial isolation, enzyme optimization, fabrication of a nanobiocatalyst, and its application. Key points • A novel isolate, Proteus mirabilis, was employed for the production of the extremozyme laccase. • Optimization increased the yield by 9.58-fold. • Bio-SeNPs were employed to degrade cypermethrin, achieving 100% detoxification within 72 h.

works.title: Colorimetric polymerase spiral reaction (PSR) assay for the rapid detection of hepatitis B virus
works.abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant global health concern, particularly in low-resource settings with limited access to sophisticated diagnostic tools. Conventional molecular diagnostic assays, such as qPCR, are often restricted to centralized laboratories in urban settings due to their high cost and the need for skilled personnel. This limits its use in lower levels of the healthcare system, highlighting the need for affordable point-of-care (PoC) assays. In this study, we have developed a visual detection method for HBV using a polymerase spiral reaction (PSR) incorporated with hydroxy naphthol blue (HNB) dye. A set of primers was designed targeting a specific region of the S gene of HBV, and the reaction runs in an isothermal condition. The assay conditions were optimized, and the optimal reaction temperature and time were 63 °C and 60 min, respectively. This developed HBV-PSR assay showed a detection limit of 5.04 copies, reaching 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity in clinical evaluation ( n = 85), and colorimetric visualization in 60 min by naked eye. The specificity test revealed no cross-reactivity with other hepatitis-causing viruses and the tested non-HBV pathogens. The assay was tested with 45 HBV-positive clinical samples, which were initially screened by a serological test, and showed a good concordance rate and diagnostic reliability. The HBV-PSR assay designed in this study could potentially be used as a point-of-care diagnostic tool for HBV detection, aiming at early surveillance and detection, focusing on healthcare in poor-resource settings. The combination of isothermal amplification with dye-based visual detection eliminated the need for complex instruments, enabling PoC detection. Key points • A rapid and sensitive PSR assay was developed for HBV detection, with results obtained within 1 h . • HNB dye enabled naked eye visual detection without the need for complex equipment . • The assay detected as few as 5.04 DNA copies and demonstrated high diagnostic performance, outperforming conventional PCR in the evaluated clinical samples .

works.title: Hydrodynamic design space for process transfer across different bioreactor platforms
works.abstract: Abstract The increasing diversification of bioreactor platforms in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including stirred-tank, 1-D rocking, and orbital-rocking systems, has created challenges for transferring processes across systems with fundamentally different mixing mechanisms. Conventional scale-up parameters, such as power input per unit volume (P/V), are well established for stirred-tank reactors (STRs), but impeller-based methods for estimating P/V are not directly applicable to impeller-free systems. In this study, a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based framework was developed to define a hydrodynamic design space for process transfer across stirred-tank (STR), 1-D rocking (RM20), and orbital-rocking (CELBIC50) bioreactor systems. Power dissipation per unit volume (Pd/V) was proposed as a platform-independent energy dissipation parameter and combined with shear stress and mixing time to define feasible operating regions. Using this framework, operating conditions could be identified across different bioreactor types using a multi-constraint hydrodynamic design space. Hydrodynamic analysis revealed distinct flow characteristics among the bioreactors, with CELBIC50 exhibiting lower mean shear stress (0.012 vs. 0.019 Pa) and a shorter mixing time (80.9 vs. 146.6 s) than RM20 under the selected operating conditions. Despite these differences, fed-batch CHO cell cultures under the selected conditions showed comparable cell growth, productivity, metabolite profiles, and product quality across STR 2 L, RM20, and CELBIC50, with most performance variables remaining within the common ± 2 σ range. These results demonstrate that a multi-constraint hydrodynamic design space integrating Pd/V, shear stress, and mixing time provides a quantitative framework for identifying transferable operating conditions across different bioreactor systems and supports model-informed process development. Key points • Hydrodynamic characteristics were systematically compared across stirred-tank, 1-D rocking-motion, and orbital-rocking bioreactors under diverse operating conditions. • Pd/V was proposed as a platform-independent energy dissipation parameter across different bioreactor systems. • A constraint-based hydrodynamic design space integrating Pd/V, shear stress, and mixing time was developed for systematic bioprocess transfer.

works.title: High-density fermentation of Streptococcus suis serotype 31 for inactivated vaccine production
works.abstract: Streptococcus suis serotype 31 (SS31) is a clinically important swine pathogen for which inactivated vaccine development requires a scalable cultivation process and evidence that the resulting bacterin has protective activity. However, conventional culture processes often yield insufficient biomass, whereas aggressive high-density fermentation may perturb the physiological features that determine vaccine quality. Herein, we demonstrate a Response Surface Methodology (RSM)-guided fermentation-to-vaccine strategy that optimizes the SS31 culture microenvironment and evaluates the protective activity of a bacterin produced under the optimized conditions. Single-factor screening and Box-Behnken modeling identified glucose, organic nitrogen and newborn bovine serum as dominant growth variables, leading to an optimized formulation containing 2.19 g/L glucose, 43.8 g/L organic nitrogen and 5.89% serum. When scaled to a 14-L bioreactor with residual sugar controlled at 1–3 g/L and pH maintained at 7.2, this process achieved 1.51 × 10¹⁰ CFU/mL, approximately seven-fold higher than shake-flask cultivation. The LD₅₀ estimates were 2.50 × 10⁶ CFU/mouse for SS31 cultured in the optimized medium and 2.14 × 10⁷ CFU/mouse for SS31 cultured in Martin medium, indicating a difference in the virulence-associated phenotype under the experimental conditions. These estimates do not demonstrate the conservation or enhancement of vaccine antigens. Among the four vaccine formulations tested, the aluminum-adjuvanted vaccine containing 3 × 10⁹ pre-inactivation CFU equivalents/mL yielded the highest observed survival (10/10 mice) after challenge with 2 LD₅₀. The organ bacterial-load and histopathological findings were evaluated descriptively. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of the SS31 cultivation process at the 14-L scale and support further evaluation of the resulting inactivated vaccine against S. suis .

works.title: Dracaena angolesnsis leaf extract as a botanical mosquitocide: bioefficacy against Aedes aegypti, voltage-gated sodium channel (kdr) gene expression, and ecotoxicological evaluation in Danio rerio
works.abstract: Vector-borne diseases transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes remain a major global public health concern. With the growing incidence of insecticide resistance and the potential environmental hazards posed by chemical insecticides, the development of effective green and eco-friendly alternatives to chemical products for the control of mosquito-borne diseases is of paramount importance. The objective of this research work was to investigate the mosquitocidal activities of Dracaena angolesnsis leaves and associated expression of resistance-related genes and their toxicity against Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. Phytochemical screening revealed the presence of several bioactive compounds, including flavonoids, phenols, terpenoids, sterols, tannins, and alkaloids, which are known for their insecticidal potential. Larvicidal, pupicidal, and adulticidal bioassays demonstrated significant mosquito mortality across different solvent extracts, with aqueous and methanol extracts exhibiting the highest efficacy. The lowest larval LC₅₀ value was observed for the aqueous extract (12.97 ppm), while strong pupicidal and adulticidal activities were also recorded. RT-qPCR analysis of the voltage-gated sodium channel (kdr) transcript revealed marked upregulation in treated larvae, with expression levels increasing from 90.65-fold to 10,524-fold relative to untreated control larvae from the same laboratory-maintained field strain. Complete adult mortality (100%) was recorded at 250 and 500 ppm following a 24 h recovery period, and high larval mortality (91.2 ± 1.8% at 24 h, reaching 100% by 48 h at 500 ppm) was achieved despite the significant induction of kdr transcripts, indicating that the multi-target botanical extract effectively suppressed mosquito survival. However, 100% mortality of larvae was observed despite high Knockdown resistance, indicating that the extract was effective in overcoming the resistance-related defense mechanisms. In order to evaluate the environmental safety of the extract, non-target toxicity was investigated in adult zebrafish ( Danio rerio ) exposed to concentrations ranging from 31.25 to 500 ppm over a 96 h period. The extract elicited only mild, concentration-dependent behavioural alterations at the highest tested concentration (500 ppm) including transient changes in swimming orientation and social schooling with zero mortality or structural deformities recorded across all tested concentrations. These results indicate that D. angolesnsis has a high potential to be used as an insecticidal plant for mosquito control.

works.title: Immobilized bacterial consortium alleviates oxidative stress in juvenile African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) exposed to bisphenol-contaminated water
works.abstract: Health concerns about bisphenol A have prompted its replacement with analogues, bisphenol F (BPF) and bisphenol S (BPS). Regrettably, there is paucity of data on potential health hazards of these analogues while research on their removal from aqueous media is still emerging. In this study, effects of BPF and BPS exposure at sublethal concentration and bioremediation treatment were investigated on biochemical, hematological and histological parameters of selected organs (gills, liver, kidney, muscle and brain) of juvenile African catfish. 10% (10%) immobilized bisphenol-utilizing bacterial consortium was used for bioremediation treatment. Malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were assayed as an indicator of lipid peroxidation and oxidative stress. Activities of key antioxidant enzymes including superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), glutathione peroxidase (Gpx) and glutathione S transferase (GST), as well as concentration of non-enzymatic antioxidant reduced glutathione (GSH) were determined. Brain acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity was evaluated as a biomarker of environmental stress. Histological analyses of selected fish tissues were conducted across all groups. Study was carried out in triplicates and results from treated groups were compared with those of the control group. Levels of malondialdehyde and glutathione peroxidase significantly increased in polluted groups while activities of superoxide dismutase, catalase, glutathione S transferase, acetylcholinesterase, and concentration of reduced glutathione significantly decreased in the pollution groups when compared with control. Remarkably, enzyme activities in treated groups were similar to results obtained in the control groups. Lesions observed in fish tissues of polluted group were minimal in treated groups. Hematological parameters which were significantly reduced in pollution group were elevated in treated groups. Findings provide evidence-based decisions for selecting immobilized microbes as bioremediation tools, and suggest the efficacy of bioremediation treatment in alleviating BPF and BPS toxicity in fish species.

works.title: Transcriptome-guided identification of YALI0_F02013g and YALI0_A19910g as candidate NADPH-dependent oxidoreductases associated with enhanced erythritol production in Yarrowia lipolytica
works.abstract: NADPH competition by non-erythrose-reductase oxidoreductases limits erythritol yields in Yarrowia lipolytica , yet the specific contributors remain poorly defined. This study characterised two candidate genes, YALI0_F02013g (putative pyridoxine 4-dehydrogenase) and YALI0_A19910g (putative glycerol 2-dehydrogenase), using time-resolved transcriptomics, molecular docking and metabolic modelling. RNA-seq analysis across 96 h of fermentation revealed distinct temporal profiles: YALI0_F02013g was progressively induced 3.4-fold (peak 5040 FPKM at 72 h), while YALI0_A19910g was repressed 920-fold by 96 h (Table 2). Expression trends were validated by qRT-PCR (Pearson r > 0.94; Table 3). YALI0_A19910g expression correlated strongly negatively with erythritol titre (Pearson r = − 0.858), whereas YALI0_F02013g showed a weak positive correlation. Molecular docking predicted high NADPH binding affinities for both enzymes (− 9.8 and − 8.6 kcal mol⁻ 1 , respectively; Fig. 2) and identified conserved catalytic triads. An integrated prioritisation model ranked YALI0_F02013g as the higher-priority target (5.6/10 vs 5.0/10; Table 7). In silico flux estimates suggest that repressing YALI0_F02013g could conserve approximately 67% of the competing NADPH demand, potentially increasing erythritol yield by ~14%; these projections require experimental validation (Table 8). These findings identify YALI0_F02013g as a candidate metabolic bottleneck in the strain background examined, offering a specific target for engineering improved cofactor efficiency in industrial Yarrowia lipolytica strains.

works.title: CO2 availability shapes acetate and ethanol production in Clostridium aceticum: a transcriptomics-guided study
works.abstract: Clostridium aceticum , a model acetogen utilizing the Wood–Ljungdahl pathway (WLP), offers a promising microbial platform for converting CO 2 -rich syngas into value-added biofuels. In this study, we systematically investigated the effects of varying CO 2 concentrations on fermentation kinetics and global transcriptional responses of C. aceticum . Acetate production increased steadily with higher CO 2 levels, reaching 12.3 g/L at 45% CO 2 , whereas ethanol accumulation peaked at 25% CO 2 , suggesting a metabolic trade-off between acid and alcohol formation. Elevated CO 2 enhanced biomass formation and product titer, but accelerated acidification, thereby constraining cell growth at very high concentrations. Comparative transcriptomics revealed 246 differentially expressed genes, with key CO 2 fixation genes ( acsA1 and fdhF ) and ethanol biosynthesis genes ( ald and adh ) upregulated, while ATP-dependent steps of the WLP, such as fhs , were repressed, reflecting intrinsic energy limitations. Notably, the upregulation of L-serine dehydratase and formate-acetyltransferase implicated serine metabolism as an alternative route to acetyl-CoA, providing formate and CO 2 to support the WLP. Guided by these insights, exogenous L-serine supplementation increased intracellular ATP by 1.95-fold, and enhanced acetate and ethanol titer by 23.3% and 12.5%, respectively. These findings highlight CO 2 availability as a central regulator of carbon flux and energy metabolism in C. aceticum and propose amino acid supplementation as a practical strategy to improve syngas fermentation efficiency.

works.title: CRISPR/Cas9 induced disruption of oca2 and tyr genes associated with pigmentation in Danio rerio
works.abstract: Targeted disruption of genes has been successfully carried out in several model and non-model fish species. In ornamental fish industries, Danio rerio (D. rerio) represents the most significant fish species and is available in several color varieties. Recently, CRISPR/Cas9 has been used to disrupt pigmented genes in several fish species, including D. rerio . However, there have been few reports on the use of CRISPR/Cas9 for the disruption of pigmented genes tyrosinase (tyr) and oculocutaneous albinism II ( oca2 ) in D. rerio to date. In this study, guide RNA (gRNA) constructs specific to the tyr (T1) and oca2 (T2) genes were designed and synthesized, while Cas9 mRNA was synthesized through in vitro transcription. Subsequently, both the Cas9 mRNA and the gRNA constructs were validated using gel electrophoresis and sequencing. The validated Cas9 mRNA and gRNA mixture was then co-microinjected into D. rerio embryos at the 1–2 cell stage, which were obtained through natural spawning and later reared under controlled conditions. The results of gel electrophoresis and sequencing confirmed the successful synthesis and validation of the T1 and T2 targeting Cas9 mRNA and gRNA constructs. Melanophores were reduced when the T1 and T2 genes were disrupted, according to phenotypic studies of the Fo and F1 mutants, leading to visible pigmentation alterations. Furthermore, the validated gene editing constructs developed in this study may serve as useful tools for targeted pigmentation modification in other ornamental fish species, thereby supporting the development of high-value ornamental strains and advancing genetic improvement programs in aquaculture. However, further studies are required at the molecular level to confirm the mutation by genotyping.

works.title: High-throughput fabrication of HAMA/matrigel core-shell hydrogel microspheres by droplet microfluidics for in vitro NSCLC model
works.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) in vitro tumor models are increasingly used to better recapitulate key structural features of solid tumors than conventional two-dimensional culture systems. However, the high-throughput fabrication of uniform 3D tumor constructs remains challenging. Here, we report a droplet microfluidic platform for the high-throughput generation of tumor-laden core-shell microspheres. The platform consists of a three-channel microfluidic device, with Matrigel as the core phase and HAMA as the shell phase. Through coaxial flow and oil-phase shearing, core-shell droplets were generated and subsequently stabilized by blue-light photocrosslinking of the HAMA shell. By adjusting the flow rates of the core, shell, and oil phases, we obtained core-shell microspheres with controllable size and good uniformity. Under optimized conditions, including core and shell flow rates of 10:10 µL/min, an oil flow rate of 200 µL/min, and 4% HAMA, the platform generated microspheres with diameters of approximately 450 μm and enabled the construction of an in vitro NSCLC microsphere model.We then performed an initial characterization of the resulting constructs, including morphology, cell viability, and response to a model anticancer drug. Compared with a conventional 3D culture approach, the core-shell microspheres showed improved structural integrity and supported cell survival over the tested culture period. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of this microfluidic fabrication strategy for producing tumor-laden core-shell microspheres and suggest its potential as a basis for future in vitro tumor modeling and drug-response studies.

works.title: Structural variant detection across sequencing technologies
works.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are a major source of genomic diversity, yet their discovery remains challenging due to repetitive genomic contexts, alignment ambiguity and the trade-off between sequencing cost and read length. Here we introduce HitSV, which implements repetitiveness- and signature-density-aware breakpoint recognition coupled with precise haplotype-resolved local assembly, thereby enabling base-resolution SV reconstruction and genotyping in various sequencing technologies. On the HG002 benchmark, HitSV achieved 15-72% (long read), 10-36% (short read) and 12% (hybrid sequencing), respectively, higher genotype F1 scores than state-of-the-art SV callers. Applied to the 1KGP phase 4 cohort, HitSV expanded the SV callset by 31.5%, substantially reshaping allele-frequency landscapes. In a large Chinese long-read cohort, HitSV uncovered tandem-repeat-mobile-element composite arrays as a prevalent, multi-allelic class of complex SVs, highlighting composite repeat architectures as an important and previously underrecognized contributor to human structural variation.

works.title: Evolutionary logic and biotechnological potential of alternative splicing in higher eukaryotes: Comparative insights from plants and animals
Genomic and phenotypic characterization of Vibrio proteolyticus and its postbiotic potential
works.abstract: Abstract Vibrio proteolyticus DCF12.2, isolated from the intestinal tract of the flatfish Dicologlossa cuneata , was characterized through integrated genomic and phenotypic analyses to assess its antimicrobial activity, biosynthetic potential and resistance- and virulence-related features. Genome-based analyses supported its assignment to V. proteolyticus and identified biosynthetic gene clusters associated with arylpolyene, nonribosomal peptide (NRP)-metallophore/amphibactin, ectoine and ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptide/nonribosomal peptide synthetase (RiPP-/NRPS)-like pathways, together with numerous predicted antimicrobial peptide candidates. The resistome was mainly composed of chromosomal efflux- and target-associated determinants, whereas virulence-related hits were largely restricted to functions linked to motility, chemotaxis and secretion. The genome also contained sequences homologous to proteins previously described in Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida and Vibrio harveyi , as well as three prophage regions and multiple genomic islands (GIs). Phenotypic assays showed that the strain and/or its extracellular products (ECPs) inhibited P. damselae subsp. damselae , V. harveyi and Aeromonas hydrophila . The inhibitory activity of the ECPs against P. damselae subsp. damselae was maintained after incubation at 37 °C and after acidification to pH 5. In conclusion, although the strain exhibits antimicrobial activity and other characteristics that would qualify it a probiotic candidate, the presence of certain virulence factors makes it more suitable for use as a postbiotic. Key points DCF12.2 shows broad genomic potential for antimicrobial compound production Extracellular products inhibit relevant aquatic bacterial pathogens Virulence-related traits support postbiotic rather than probiotic use

works.title: Interkingdom communication 2.0: pheromone-based control between Bacillus subtilis and Saccharomyces cerevisiae
works.abstract: Microbial communities found in nature are complex and thrive in harmony, consisting of organisms derived from several kingdoms. Hence, they need to be able to communicate by quorum-sensing molecules to co-exist in close proximity. Being able to engineer artificial interkingdom communication for biotechnological approaches, such as degradation of complex biomaterials in one fermenter using controlled signaling between microorganisms, would be beneficial. Therefore, we wanted to establish a proof of principle by enabling the Gram-positive bacterium Bacillus subtilis to communicate in a controlled manner with the eukaryotic yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae by exploiting the yeast's pheromone system. We genetically modified B. subtilis to heterologously produce the α-pheromone after bacitracin induction, which in turn would activate the production of the green fluorescent protein mNeongreen upon pheromone recognition by S. cerevisiae. Co-cultivation in modified growth medium and induction of pheromone expression was successful and repeatable. Yeast activation and production of mNeongreen was visible not only by analysis but also by epifluorescence microscopy of the co-culture. This study successfully demonstrated controlled interkingdom signaling between microorganisms by leveraging their native communication systems. KEY POINTS: • Heterologous production and secretion of small peptides in Bacillus subtilis. • Interkingdom communication between bacteria and yeast. • Signaling by artificially produced pheromones.

works.title: Butyrate production from the simultaneous utilization of carbon monoxide and acetate in Eubacterium-dominated enrichments
works.abstract: Abstract Syngas conversion to carboxylic acids can be achieved through the combined actions of acetogens and chain elongators. Mixed cultures enriched with these functional groups can serve as robust and resilient catalysts for bio-based production, but developing efficient and stable communities remains challenging. In this study, we aimed to enrich a mixed microbial culture for efficient syngas-driven chain elongation using carbon monoxide (CO) and acetate as substrates. Three strategies were employed: (i) conventional enrichment using anaerobic sludge only, (ii) sludge augmentation with known syngas fermenters (Clostridium autoethanogenum, Clostridium carboxidivorans, Eubacterium limosum, and Acetobacterium wieringae) to enhance carboxydotrophic activity, and (iii) sludge augmentation with chain elongator Clostridium kluyveri to stimulate chain elongation. Enrichments were performed in batch cultures with stepwise increases in CO partial pressure across successive transfers until a 100% CO (170 kPa) headspace was reached. Ultimately, all enrichments grew under a 100% CO headspace, simultaneously utilizing CO and acetate, with butyrate as main product. 16S rRNA gene and metagenomic analyses revealed that Eubacterium became predominant. Several genera (Aminobacterium, Anaerotignum, Oscillibacter, and Proteiniphilum) not known to ferment CO, were also enriched. Based on physiological and metagenomic analyses, we hypothesize that Eubacterium consumes CO and acetate, producing butyrate and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS)-like material. Metagenomic data further suggests that components derived from this EPS-like material may serve as substrate for the other enriched genera. This study demonstrates that augmentation can steer mixed microbial communities toward targeted product formation and highlights the critical role of initial culture conditions in shaping community composition and functionality. Key points • Mixed cultures converted CO and acetate mainly to butyrate under a 100% CO headspace. • Acetogen augmentation to a mixed community shortened lag-phase in the presence of CO. • Metagenomics suggests microbial use of sugars and amino acids from EPS-like material.

works.title: Current status of genetic engineering for sophorolipids production
works.abstract: Sophorolipids are a family of microbial biosurfactants that contain a hydrophilic sophorose head and a hydrophobic fatty acid tail. Sophorolipids have gained prominence within both academia and the commercial biochemical industry due to their potential as a more sustainable and functional substitute for petroleum-based surfactants in many applications, both traditional and novel. However, the sophorolipids market competitiveness and economic viability face significant challenges from the current level of production performance, production costs, as well as selectivity of sophorolipids forms and their associated functional properties. Genetic engineering of the producer organisms, such as the workhorse Starmerella bombicola and others, could be a powerful tool to improve various aspects of sophorolipids production, including sophorolipids: titers, yields, productivities, novel forms, product selectivity, improved utilization of novel or sustainable fermentation feedstocks, process scalability, and process intensification. This review is designed to provide a focused look at the current status of genetic engineering for sophorolipids production, including assessments of notable studies on the generation of recombinant sophorolipid producers, their specific aims and achievements, as well as their associated challenges and knowledge gaps to be addressed. Additionally, further discussions on how the genetic engineering toolbox and physiological understandings of sophorolipid producers need to be further improved are also provided. The perspectives, discussions, and recommendations provided should aid future research and development endeavors to further improve the genetic engineering of sophorolipids producers, sophorolipids bioprocess development, and their further commercialization.

Metabolic engineering of Klebsiella oxytoca for highly selective meso-2,3-butanediol production with minimized byproducts
Rare earth element biosensing in chemically complex waters: Interference mechanisms, operating windows, and mitigation for a lanmodulin enzymatic switch
works.abstract: Rare earth elements (REE) are increasingly mobilised from mine residues and other industrial sources, creating a need for rapid screening of chemically complex waters where conventional ICP-based analysis is impractical on site. Here, we evaluate a lanthanide-gated enzymatic switch biosensor, for matrix-aware monitoring of mine-influenced waters. We quantified REE-dependent activation and systematic interference from co-occurring metals and anions typical of mine waters, and defined operating windows that preserve lanthanide responsiveness. REE activation was readily detectable at ~100 nM, whereas inhibition emerged in the low-micromolar range and became pronounced near ~10 µM for key interferents, corresponding to a practical tolerance of roughly 1:100 (REE:inhibiting element). Inhibition was strongest for Al III , Fe III , Ga III , Zn II , and Sn II . Combined machine learning, molecular dynamics, and density functional theory analyses indicate distinct inhibition modes, including coordination of Fe III , Zn II , and Sn II at the LanM EF4 hand loop and favourable binding of [Al(OH) 4 ] - /[Ga(OH) 4 ] - near the TEM-1 substrate-recognition region. Consistent with these predictions, citrate reduced inhibition from hydrolysing metals, especially Al III and Sn II . Together, these findings define matrix-dependent operating envelopes, mechanistic design rules, and practical mitigation strategies for deploying REE biosensors in chemically complex waters.

works.title: Comparison of synthetic and post-synthetic molecular genetic methods of reducing xylan glucuronidation in hybrid aspen for biorefinery applications
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: The pattern of xylan backbone substitution by 4-O-methylglucuronic acid (mGlcA) and O-acetyl groups generated during biosynthesis in the Golgi apparatus plays a key role in molecular interactions between secondary cell wall polymers in hardwoods, thus regulating biorefinery properties of woody biomass. This study aims at comparing the effects of two different approaches to reduce xylan glucuronidation, targeting either xylan biosynthesis by RNAi suppression of GLUCURONIC SUBSTITUTION OF XYLAN1 genes (denoted Gux1RNAi) or by xylan post-synthetic modification in the secondary cell wall by apoplastic wood-specific expression of a fungal α-glucuronidase from family GH67 (denoted WP:GH67) in hybrid aspen (Populus tremula L. x tremuloides Michx.). The effects of reducing xylan glucuronidation by these two approaches on xylan acetylation and solubility, and recalcitrance of wood to enzymatic hydrolysis were compared. RESULTS: Both approaches reduced mGlcA/xylose (Xyl) ratio by approx. 30% without altering Xyl content in alkali extracts, while xylan acetyl content in subcritical water extracts was increased only in Gux1RNAi lines. The Gux1RNAi lines showed reduced glucuronidation in the major xylan domain containing evenly-spaced mGlcA, whereas the WP:GH67 lines were affected in both odd and even glucuronidation patterns. Interestingly, the arrays containing mGlcA every second xylosyl unit were not affected by any modification, whereas an increase in xylo-oligosaccharides containing O-2,3 diacetylated Xyl was found in Gux1RNAi lines only. Neither modification consistently affected glucose or Xyl yields in saccharification without or with acid pretreatment, whereas xylan extractability in subcritical water was increased in Gux1RNAi, but not in WP:GH67 lines. CONCLUSION: Our study supports the hypothesis that acetylation competes with glucuronidation by GUX1 during biosynthesis, and increased acetylation caused by GUX1 suppression rather than reduced xylan glucuronidation per se improves xylan extractability. The 30% reduction in glucuronidation did not affect enzymatic saccharification, supporting the concept that cell wall structure and recalcitrance in transgenic lines are maintained by xylan domains which were not affected by either transgenic modification.

works.title: Metabolic engineering of Methylorubrum extorquens PA1 for cinnamic acid production from ethanol
works.abstract: Developing a microbial platform capable of converting ethanol into value-added products is vital for next-generation carbon recycling biorefineries. Methylorubrum extorquens PA1 is a facultative methylotroph that assimilates ethanol; however, its metabolic potential for aromatic synthesis from ethanol has not been explored. Here, we report the first demonstration of de novo cinnamic acid (CA) production from ethanol in a methylotrophic bacterium. Metabolite profiling revealed that ethanol assimilation was limited by inefficient conversion of acetate to acetyl-CoA. Overexpression of endogenous acetyl-CoA synthase (MeACS1) suppressed extracellular acetate accumulation and improved growth on ethanol. To establish the CA biosynthetic module, we introduced Streptomyces maritimus phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (SmEncP), enabling conversion of L-phenylalanine into CA. To enhance precursor supply, we strengthened the shikimate pathway and phenylalanine biosynthetic pathway by co-expressing feedback-resistant 3-deoxy-D-arabino-heptulosonate-7-phosphate synthase (EcAroG fbr ) and chorismate mutase/prephenate dehydrogenase (EcPheA fbr ) from Escherichia coli . Further, endogenous transketolase (MeTkt) was overexpressed to enhance erythrose-4-phosphate supply. The resulting strain PAc1/pTE102-CA3 produced 1.75 mg L⁻ 1 of CA from ethanol in test tube culture, 2.6-fold that obtained from methanol. Fed-batch cultivation with ethanol feeding achieved 52.34 mg L⁻ 1 of CA, demonstrating stable conversion of ethanol to value-added chemicals without notable growth inhibition or acetate accumulation. This study establishes M. extorquens PA1 as a promising chassis for ethanol-based aromatic biosynthesis and suggests that relieving acetyl-CoA bottlenecks is likely critical for efficient ethanol assimilation. This work provides ethanol-driven aromatic biosynthesis in methylotrophs and offers a foundation for further engineering of C₂-assimilating bacteria toward renewable chemical production.

Abstract
                     Cytochrome P450 reductases (CPRs) are microsomal diflavin oxidoreductases that transfer electrons from nicotinamide cofactors to class II cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs). CPRs can also reduce other proteins, including cytochrome b5, heme oxygenase, and components of the fatty acid elongation system, as well as nonphysiological acceptors such as cytochrome c, ferricyanide, and various drugs.
